1.Text: You found Chronos... sank your fangs into his throat. Sister Hecate gave me the gist. How'd you do it...? Found some exploitable weakness, something like that?

2.Text: Mostly I just kept evading a lot. He's very powerful, but must have underestimated my ability to resist his tricks.

3.Text: He won't always underestimate you, though. Must have his vulnerabilities. {#Emph}The old are seldom wise, and often weak{#Prev}, right? He's bloodied... go for the kill.

1.Text: You're close, aren't you? To putting Chronos down for good. I know you mustn't share the details even with me, but... you'd tell me if I'm wrong.

2.Text: I'd tell you, yes. Now then, I hate to make our meetings brief, but I've a certain matter to resolve.

3.Text: Then go resolve it, by all means. Tread softly, and strike true, Sister.

1.Text: Those blades of yours doing you any good? Let me know if you need any, {#Emph}erm... pointers...?

2.Text: The Sister Blades are almost like having you by my side in every fight. Though, you can shoot a lot farther than I can throw...

3.Text: {#Emph}Oh{#Prev}, don't be so hard on yourself, I can shoot farther than anybody! Especially Apollo. Well, just keep going for their vitals, and you'll be fine.

1.Text: Look at {#Emph}you{#Prev}, Sister! Your brother once had us all convinced he was trying to fight his way to Olympus. Now none of us can believe you're trying to do it for real.

2.Text: I've known Hermes about as long as you, and can count the number of favors he's asked of me on one hand. Besides, I could use the change of scenery.

3.Text: Then by all means! What a time, that you're on your way up to the mountain while I'm on my way down to the Underworld. At least we crossed paths!

1.Text: Look at {#Emph}you{#Prev}, Sister! Your brother once had us all convinced he was trying to fight his way to Olympus. Now none of us can believe you're trying to do it for real.

2.Text: Hermes wouldn't have asked me to go if it wasn't important. Besides, I could use the change of scenery.

3.Text: Then by all means! What a time, that you're on your way up to the mountain while I'm on my way down to the Underworld. At least we crossed paths!

1.Text: Poor wretches, left to linger here. Could be relaxing in Elysium, or Asphodel at least. No wonder they're upset.

2.Text: Chronos claimed it was an act of magnanimity, unsealing the Underworld gates, letting the dead roam free. This can't possibly be better than when my father ruled.

3.Text: Hey, at least it means I can set foot in these parts without inciting some huge territorial dispute! Setting aside the fact that we're already in the middle of one.

1.Text: You probably know {#Emph}Eris {#Prev}has been buzzing around Olympus recently? One good lightning bolt from Father Zeus would normally take {#Emph}care {#Prev}of that, but... he's been occupied.

2.Text: One good lightning bolt, how about one good arrow? We'd be saved a lot of trouble if Eris were to be plucked from the sky one of these nights.

3.Text: I'd gladly volunteer, it's just that Father has everything {#Emph}well under control. {#Prev}Says I'm needed way out here instead. But if I do spot the wings of Strife... they're going down.

1.Text: Hey you have an animal companion now! Mine would be with me too, except they won't set foot in the Underworld while they still draw breath... except these birds, which do not seem to care.

2.Text: And I suppose they have other excuses for Ephyra? Some companions they are, leaving you to your devices here.

3.Text: {#Emph}Hah! {#Prev}They're just like us for the most part, except quieter usually. You take good care of yours for me, all right?

1.Text: You've been so far from home for so long. Don't you miss being on Olympus? If not now, then... back before the Titan's siege?

2.Text: What, you mean being with my father and stepmother, my perfect twin brother, and all the rest? Just because I'm willing to aid them doesn't mean I'm willing to live with them again.

1.Text: So what do you think of the family? Most of them are stuck on their mountaintop, though... you've seen what they're like.

2.Text: Oh they don't seem so bad! Especially things being as they are. But you can't stand any of them...

3.Text: Hey I wouldn't go {#Emph}that {#Prev}far! Though, yes, they can get under my skin. They're going to owe us {#Emph}big {#Prev}once all of this is over.

1.Text: It's really true about the Fates, that Chronos somehow got to them? Doesn't want to take any chances anymore. Did the Fates prophesize their own captivity...?

2.Text: How can you be so casual about this? If the Fates themselves couldn't stop Chronos, we won't have an easy time! We're beholden to chance ourselves.

3.Text: So what if we are! You know not even {#Emph}I {#Prev}always hit my mark. What do I do if I miss? {#Emph}I take another shot. {#Prev}The greater the skill, the less is up to chance.

1.Text: You bested Sister Hecate! She told me so herself, and with dare-I-say more than a hint of pride. Though, she's intent on testing you still?

2.Text: She always said I can't beat Chronos if I can't beat her. And so we spar. I think she's gone easy on me, to boost my confidence.

3.Text: Well, I can plainly see she failed. Gone {#Emph}easy? {#Prev}If there's one thing the Witch of the Crossroads hasn't ever done, it's that.

1.Text: Seen Heracles stomping about? As much as I am normally the trusting sort, I don't quite know about that one. He's been on my bad side for a while. Quite rough with animals.

2.Text: Artemis, you're goddess of the {#Emph}hunt. {#Prev}Animals must be far more afraid of you than him.

3.Text: Now don't you even start with that, Sister. Animals {#Emph}adore {#Prev}me, except when it's their time. But Heracles goes after them whenever he needs. Just watch it with him, OK?

1.Text: Hermes finally got a hold of you, did he? Sounds like things have really taken a turn on Olympus. Glad I'm not there!

2.Text: Artemis, how can you say that? It's your home. I'm going to see if I can head up there and lend a hand.

3.Text: Is that even possible for you, born of the Underworld and all that? Then again, you're a {#Emph}witch! {#Prev}Must have a remedy for everything!

1.Text: Those are the Sister Blades... then, that must be the Aspect of the Morrigan. Looks like it suits you pretty well! Maybe we Night-Moon goddesses {#Emph}are {#Prev}all alike.

2.Text: You mean you never got to wield this Aspect yourself? How did you even learn the waking-phrase you shared?

3.Text: One too many questions, Melinoë, but no. That Aspect wasn't for me. Maybe some evening you, too, will have the opportunity to pass along some secret knowledge!

1.Text: You know, I set up Zagreus with his {#Emph}own {#Prev}waking-phrase one time, for a hidden Aspect of a bow called Coronacht, which Stepmother once used. He was pretty good with it!

2.Text: Oh {#Emph}truly? {#Prev}And what else would you say he did better than me, Artemis? Certainly he had more charm, but could he sprint faster than me, too?

3.Text: Absolutely, {#Emph}much {#Prev}faster. {#Emph}Anyway{#Prev}, the point being, I'm pleased to have seen each of you grow strong, and done my part for the Infernal and Nocturnal Arms alike.

1.Text: Brought the White Antler with you just in case! The stag who gave it up, it was his time. And I vowed to him I'd make it quick. His Shade and I, we still commune every so often!

2.Text: Artemis, your tales have this remarkable capacity to warm the heart and yet disturb the mind. In case you ever need a calling other than the hunt.

3.Text: If none of this works out, I was thinking {#Emph}songs {#Prev}and {#Emph}music-making? {#Prev}If Apollo can do it, so can {#Emph}I. {#Prev}Though we've not tired of the hunter's life just yet.

1.Text: Glad the old Antler there has served you well. Keep pushing {#Emph}that {#Prev}thing and you're liable to bring the stag who gave it up back to life! Or take over for {#Emph}me {#Prev}on the hunt.

2.Text: Oh I wouldn't want {#Emph}that... {#Prev}just to be hell-bent on repeatedly hitting my foes in their vital regions. And for some reason your White Antler helps!

3.Text: {#Emph}Some reason? {#Prev}Our {#Emph}bond's {#Prev}the reason, and the Antler's the connection. Just don't get carried away. I take most shots while out of sight, but {#Emph}you {#Prev}are not as shy.

1.Text: Why has Olympus sent you all the way out here, anyway? I thought you'd have gone back by now. You're always welcome in the Crossroads!

2.Text: Appreciate it, Sister, and I do have to report back soon enough. As for why I'm all the way out here, mostly to spy on you! Olympus likes to be informed.

3.Text: I'm certain that they do. Do you ever slip up with them? By now the other gods must have their suspicions about you and Hermes.

4.Text: Depends on who you're talking about I guess, but for the most part they just think we're young and flighty. But we're the best they've got.

1.Text: So when you're not aiding me in my repeated failures, what else have you been up to, Artemis? Some special quarry you're after?

2.Text: There might be. Olympus has been shaking, for reasons unknown. Sister Selene asked that I look into it. Surely it's nothing, right?

1.Text: A full Moon... Sister Selene's power at its peak. On nights like this, I really feel my immortality. May our combined strength be enough.
Hey, is it really true Moros himself showed up at your Crossroads because you {#Emph}summoned {#Prev}him? As in, you {#Emph}literally invited Doom...?

2.Text: It doesn't seem the wisest course when you put it that way. Chronos once was brought low by a prophecy of the Three Fates. I felt they might be willing to intervene again.

3.Text: And they did so by sending you the embodiment of misfortune and unforeseen consequences. Well if that's what the Fates have in store, you're going to need {#Emph}this.

1.Text: You haven't seen Nemesis tonight, have you? Not that she should be anywhere near here, as opposed to keeping watch over the gateways at the Crossroads.

2.Text: I haven't seen her, no. But I was tracking her! Those footprints are only slightly harder to spot than {#Emph}she {#Prev}is. She's not supposed to be out here, is she...

3.Text: ...That she is not. She's just trying to make herself useful, I get it. And the Fates themselves know that I could probably use the help. Though, how have you two been?

4.Text: We each need company, we each need solitude, the same old thing. She's frustrated, which can go a couple of ways depending on the night. Anyway, she's a big girl!

1.Text: Hey Artemis, if Nemesis and I... if we were closer, would that be all right? I mean with {#Emph}you. {#Prev}Because if not, just say the word. It's probably not going anywhere anyway...

2.Text: What am I, Sister Hecate? You don't need my permission, not like Nemesis belongs to me, though I've considered trapping her. In all seriousness, good hunting with that one.

1.Text: So how has Nemesis been doing, she all right? Seems to finally be getting farther in her own stubborn attempts.

2.Text: Oh she's been well, for her. We've been seeing each other more, and... it's good. As good as she can probably permit.

3.Text: That's great! She did seem a little lighter on her feet, but not {#Emph}too {#Prev}light, of course. You'll have to tell me how you got through her defenses sometime.

1.Text: Fine mess we made! Not many hiding-places here compared to Erebus. Might be the end of the line for me... I'm a huntress, not a fisher.

2.Text: Fishing is a form of hunting, isn't it? Anyway I appreciate the backup, and understand if you're now at the limit of your range. Olympus probably expects you back.

3.Text: They'll want to hear from me! About the situation, and about {#Emph}you{#Prev}, too. You know they still take me and Hermes for their spies? Although, we do tell them a lot...

1.Text: That massive Cyclops Polyphemus... saw him fast asleep the other night! Then {#Emph}you {#Prev}were able to sneak up and incapacitate him, just like {#Emph}that! {#Prev}I stay far downwind of him, myself.

2.Text: I'm tempted to just smile and nod through this one, Artemis, but my dealings with the Cyclops haven't involved much stealth. Though at least I can get past him, at this point.

3.Text: And how do you get through the Rift beyond the docks, you {#Emph}swim? {#Prev}You still like doing things the hard way. The {#Emph}only {#Prev}way!

1.Text: Any progress yet with your investigation?

2.Text: Not near as much as I'd like. Here, let me give you a boost. Maybe you'll get somewhere even if I don't.

1.Text: You saw we're up against Prometheus. His whole thing is how he knows what's going to take place... makes him quite an elusive one, I guess.

2.Text: The Titan of Foresight, fighting for the Titan of Time... perhaps merely against the gods who punished him. He may have his reasons, but he's in my way.

3.Text: I know precisely what you mean. Though if he really knows the future, wouldn't he choose the winning side...? Careful with him, Sister...

1.Text: One disadvantage to my being all the way out here is I'm unable to put arrows through Prometheus from such a range. Apollo says he's been a real bother.

2.Text: He's a problem and a threat... even unarmed, and seemingly not even at full strength, for he still bears old wounds. He has more than enough fury to make up.

3.Text: Great, another angry Titan. Well if he's {#Emph}seething {#Prev}all the time, he's liable to make mistakes. It wouldn't be the first time.

1.Text: You don't truly believe Prometheus can see the future, do you? He probably just has heightened instincts like yours.

2.Text: {#Emph}Excuse me? {#Prev}Nobody has instincts as heightened as {#Emph}these{#Prev}, Sister! But I've never claimed to know {#Emph}precisely {#Prev}what's to come. Even if I could, I think I'd miss all the suspense.

1.Text: You've likely heard I didn't get there, Artemis. Didn't even come close.

2.Text: Sister, I have {#Emph}every {#Prev}faith in you, but not even {#Emph}I {#Prev}believed you were going to vanquish Chronos straightaway. Let's be a little realistic here?

1.Text: Clean and efficient, just the way I like it, Sister. Not been too much to report on my side, and it seems like things are well on yours. Let's keep it moving then, shall we?
I can often depend on Sister Selene's light to guide me on my hunts. But where you're going, she can't follow, can she? Nor can I.

2.Text: And Headmistress Hecate is needed at the Crossroads. I alone have the authority to enter the House of Hades. If I can make it there.

3.Text: Hey, what do you mean {#Emph}if? {#Prev}It's a matter of {#Emph}when{#Prev}, as far as I'm concerned. I'm thinking maybe very {#Emph}soon{#Prev}, in fact.

1.Text: I can often depend on Sister Selene's light to guide me on my hunts. But where you're going, she can't follow easily, can she? Nor can I.

2.Text: Sister Selene has her ways, though I know it's difficult for her, and Headmistress is needed at the Crossroads. I alone have the authority to enter the House of Hades. But I'd have never gotten there without you all.

3.Text: Could {#Emph}really {#Prev}use a proper hunting party for this one! Fortunately it's kind of our thing as Silver Sisters to not have to be in the same place at the same time.

1.Text: There's a particular {#Emph}chill {#Prev}in the air tonight. I almost broke a {#Emph}sweat! {#Prev}Though our foes were partly to blame. I think I know what's going on, Melinoë, but what is going {#Emph}on?

2.Text: The Testament of Night is what. The Fear and Darkness spread... which may not seem to our immediate benefit, but the Nocturnal Arms grow stronger through it; and the realm.

3.Text: Well then! {#Emph}In shadow, we serve; to shadow, we return. {#Prev}Olympus figured it was Chronos up to something. I had my doubts, but... wanted to be sure.

1.Text: I had more trouble getting here than usual. The Testament of Night again? Nyx herself would surely be impressed with all you've done, spreading {#Emph}fear{#Prev}, creating {#Emph}nightmares...

2.Text: Through fear comes respect and obedience. Once we're finished, then perhaps the next would-be usurpers with designs on either of our realms are going to think twice.

3.Text: That was a rather good impression of your father, Sister. Well, let's go terrify our foes some more, shall we?

1.Text: When I became one of the Silver Sisters, I figured all we'd really do was stalk in shadows, make occasional reports... but this is a full-on {#Emph}worst-case scenario!

2.Text: You sound excited rather than dismayed. You must have known it'd come to this eventually. Not like Headmistress would band us together just for ceremony's sake.

3.Text: No, I guess you're right. Still, we've been together biding our time for so long... I got to thinking we might never get the opportunity to strike. Yet here we are!

1.Text: Good being in the Crossroads earlier. My aim is steadier, nerves calm again. I don't get any real peace at home... but it's there to be found in the woods.

2.Text: No place to practice singing at home either, I expect. Is it truly that concerning if Apollo hears? He can't be {#Emph}that {#Prev}much better! And he'd probably be proud of you.

3.Text: Or he'd tease me incessantly... I'd likely have to put an arrow through him and get into a heap of trouble. Not prepared to take that sort of risk, Sister.

1.Text: Good being in the Crossroads earlier. My aim is steadier, nerves calm again. I don't get any real peace at home... but it's there to be found in the woods.

2.Text: You could always do some singing back at home, though, right? You're at least as good as Apollo at this point. He'd welcome your accompaniment at the Palace, I'm sure!

3.Text: Or he'd tease me incessantly... I'd likely have to put an arrow through him and get into a heap of trouble. Not prepared to take that sort of risk, Sister.

1.Text: You made it quite a ways up on the surface recently, Sister Selene said. Did it live up to all your hopes and dreams?

2.Text: I tend to have a lot of nightmares, and it did live up to those. The dead are left to linger there. They should be safely in the Underworld!

3.Text: Well, Chronos evidently has other ideas for how things should be governed. I know your main objective is below, though... thank you for any aid you can provide up top.

1.Text: So much for visiting the surface, huh? Not seen a trace of you up there! Don't feel bad. You have nice woods here, too!

2.Text: I'm not supposed to be up there... could hardly breathe. But there might be something I can do. Hermes wouldn't have asked me to go if it wasn't important.

3.Text: No, I guess not. I'd offer to escort you though Olympus wants me to stay out of sight. And I won't bother saying not to push yourself too hard...

1.Text: We're quite the team, aren't we? And that's {#Emph}without {#Prev}Sisters Hecate and Selene backing us up. Shame that we all have to spread out most of the time.

2.Text: We do have several realms to watch. But yes, I have to say it's been a pleasure working with you recently. Singing with you. Having your friendship.

3.Text: Now don't get sentimental on me, Sister. This is business. And though the world we live in may be looking a bit bleak, at least business is good.

1.Text: Not seen each other in how many nights, Sister? {#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, I know that's just the way it goes. You're busy, I'm busy, bunch of time goes by, and... here we are.

2.Text: Doubtless we've crossed paths repeatedly, just not quite close enough. I feel like a lot's transpired since last we met like this. Where to even begin?

3.Text: Oh no need, we haven't seen each other but I've still been keeping up. Olympus knows of all your latest exploits! The ones you wouldn't mind me sharing, anyway.

1.Text: We've bigger problems on Olympus than we counted on, I hear. Our worst fears realized and so on? You'd think I'd be more capable of tracking prey that's Typhon's size...

2.Text: You were tracking Chronos... me, perhaps. But if it's any consolation, finding Typhon ought to be quite easy at this point! Bringing him down... less so.

3.Text: I'll take your word for it. My father's much too proud to call me back to aid in our defense. Says I'm still needed here. If he wants Typhon to himself so badly, he can have him.

1.Text: Olympus managed to take Typhon down...? I figure with {#Emph}your {#Prev}aid, probably Sister Selene's too. I guess I wasn't needed up there after all.

2.Text: We drove the monster back, but I don't think we've properly discouraged him. Not yet, at least. Though I've a few ideas...

3.Text: If your ideas involve an {#Emph}arrow {#Prev}in his eye, of which I hear he has a {#Emph}lot{#Prev}, let me know... moonlight guide you home tonight.

1.Text: I meant to thank you, since our woods and mountains are no longer likely to be crushed beneath a monster's foot or slithering appendages. That's been a big relief.

2.Text: Oh, anytime. I wouldn't have liked being crushed that way, either. Sounds like Lord Zeus and Queen Hera had some contingency in mind that was best avoided.

3.Text: Our woods and mountains would have been in even {#Emph}worse {#Prev}shape then. Your way shook Father and Stepmother up a bit... the power to destroy immortals and all that? But it's best they respect you. That's how you get them to be nice!

1.Text: ...I hate to even ask, but... have you picked up any trace of Zagreus, by any chance, while in your father's House?

2.Text: Artemis, it's... hard for me to say. My brother isn't there, but... I sense his presence; our connection. He's not gone.

3.Text: I guess that's good enough for me, for now. Although it's much more {#Emph}cryptic {#Prev}than I'd like! Well, wherever he is... he better be all right. And not alone.

1.Text: Take this, Sister, and go find your mark.
Tread ever softly and strike swift and true, Sister.
Happened to be in the area again, so thought I'd stop on by.
May Moonlight guide you to your prey, and expose his every weakness.
Another night, another duty for the Silver Sisters.
I have to say, these woods are not my favorite...
I can't venture any further below, though I can give you this.
The skilled huntress keeps her bag of tricks full and with her at all times.
Steady yourself, Sister. You have my full support and more.
May your aim ever be true. Not unlike mine!
I still think you should try a bow again sometime...
We hunt alone. Although these run-ins aren't so bad!
Always a pleasure working with you, Sister.
Go cut that wretched Titan down to size for me, would you?
May none dare stand between a witch and her prey.
Fine night for hunting Titans, don't you think?
Picked up the scent of a few stragglers I'll take care of after this...
You'll find your mark. I know you will.
Yours is the most dangerous prey of all. I'm a bit envious!
Here's a little something to go with those witching arts of yours.
I've got your back, Sister, so just keep moving forward.
We're the Silver Sisters, and we never miss our mark.
We are the Silver Sisters, and this is our time to shine.
Got to say it's nice to get away from it all like this.
Fancy running into you again, and here of all places!
You tracked {#Emph}me {#Prev}down this time, I'll have you know!
You were born to do this, Sister, and you're going to succeed.
Sure beats being back on that mountaintop, let me tell you.
The Moon is full again. May our combined might take you far.
A new moon marks a new beginning, so take heart, Sister.
The Moon's light wanes again, but your strength needn't falter.
As the light of the waxing Moon intensifies, so too does our potential, Sister.
Good hunting on the way up to the mountain, Sister.
Father better have expressed his gratitude for all you've done.
Good of you to deal with Typhon so that we don't have to anymore!
I'll cover your tracks, but first, here's something for the road.
Next time leave more of them for me, would you?
Clean and efficient, just the way I like it, Sister.
Here, a little extra Moon magick for all you've done, and still intend to do.
It's been too long, Sister. Look at you, on your great hunt! Not ideal circumstances but you've finally begun. Know that the family has your back, surprised as they are about this.

2.Text: No shortage lately of surprises on Olympus or below. It's good to see you, Artemis. But, I must be off. Time's against us, and all that.

3.Text: {#Emph}Time{#Prev}'s an old fool too busy besieging the mountain of the gods to sense the threat headed his way. Go get him.

1.Text: We Silver Sisters, we're the keepers of the Nocturnal Arms. The blades of Lim and Oros serve Night's will at your command, but there is more to them.

2.Text: You're serious? I'm listening. What would you have me do?

3.Text: At the Silver Pool, invoke the blades with this: {#Emph}I see your threefold shadow with the Phantom Queen. {#Prev}I think you're ready now. It should be good!

4.Text: {#Emph}I see your threefold shadow with the Phantom Queen. {#Prev}A waking-phrase... thank you for the honor, Artemis. Whose Aspect is this, do you know?

5.Text: {#Emph}Oh{#Prev}, no one in particular, just another threefold goddess of shadow, like Sister Hecate but of a different age and place. I shouldn't say more, you'll see for yourself soon enough.

1.Text: It's strange... I work so closely with Sister Selene, but I've never been any good with her Hexes. Not like {#Emph}you.

2.Text: And I am woefully incompetent with bow-and-arrow, not like {#Emph}you. {#Prev}It's probably Nemesis ensuring none of us have it all.

3.Text: Well, you're about to get a little {#Emph}closer {#Prev}to that enviable point. Here, a little extra Moon magick for all you've done, and still intend to do. In case you need it.

1.Text: Oh, you look like {#Emph}hell{#Prev}, Sister. Don't have anything to patch you up, but I {#Emph}can {#Prev}help you kill the wretches that did this to you!
You're barely on your feet, Sister. Let's save our breath and concentrate on getting through the rest of this intact. Far as we can, at least.
Sorry I couldn't keep them all at bay. I try to pack a few recovery supplies, but have to travel light.
{#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, one of these evenings where nothing's gone right. Have to push through to the next! Or turn {#Emph}this {#Prev}one around.
Everybody on the mountain's going on about the Fates finally turning up. Father wouldn't even be in charge if not for them, so he must not have liked the thought that they were gone...

2.Text: But now the Fates have said the influence of gods shall wane to an extent. I can't imagine Lord Uncle Zeus and the rest are too pleased about {#Emph}that.

3.Text: No, but as major prophecies are concerned, it's really not that bad. And besides, it sounds like this new age of theirs might not be for a while, so... we'll worry about it then!

1.Text: The deed is done, or should I say the {#Emph}task {#Prev}is finally complete. But, you're right back to work!

2.Text: Yes, well... call it a habit, or an opportunity to check up on some things. And thank you, Artemis. I won't forget the flight of the Silver Sisters.

3.Text: Apollo just {#Emph}had {#Prev}to come along, though I won't soon forget it either. Not felt a victory like that in ages. Wait, why {#Emph}are {#Prev}we still fighting?

4.Text: To destroy every last trace of the threat we faced, apparently. So I still need you around as much as ever.

5.Text: You mean we get to keep {#Emph}this {#Prev}up, and I will have as much target practice as I want? Well {#Emph}OK!

1.Text: Things are better than I would have thought back home. Still odd to see us dealing with the remnants of the siege, but Father Zeus has been a lot less temperamental, finally.

2.Text: That's good to hear, and I'm glad you had the opportunity to be there yourself. So does this mean I won't be seeing you as much out here? They must want you back.

3.Text: Well, between us, they still want me to keep an eye on you, powerful witch that you are. But, I do have to check in now and again, which I don't mind. They've been glad to see {#Emph}me{#Prev}, and to hear all about {#Emph}you{#Prev}, and... I can say hi to the Nymphs!

1.Text: Hey, Artemis. Is everything all right?

2.Text: So much to talk about, so little time, Sister. I'm needed elsewhere, but I wanted to make sure to send you off.

1.Text: {#Emph}I see your threefold shadow with the Phantom Queen.
If we must.
For your journey.

2.Text: My blessings...

3.Text: For you.

4.Text: Here's what I have.

5.Text: The choice is yours.

1.Text: That's settled.

2.Text: Well met!

3.Text: Hail.

4.Text: Cousin.

5.Text: Melinoë.

1.Text: You're here!
Lady Athena...!

2.Text: Lady Athena!

3.Text: Excellent timing.

4.Text: It's her...

5.Text: Sorry to bother you...

1.Text: The fury of Olympus!

2.Text: Deliverance!

3.Text: In the name of Zeus!

4.Text: In the name of Zeus...!

5.Text: For Olympus!

1.Text: Let us be off.

2.Text: Fight on, Cousin!

3.Text: To the next battle.

4.Text: Onward, then!

5.Text: To greater victory.

1.Text: You honor me with such a gift, Goddess.
Lady Athena, while we have a moment, I wish to offer you this Nectar as a token of my gratitude. If I'd only known that we would meet here, perhaps I'd have arrived even sooner.

2.Text: Nonsense, for I'm certain that you made your journey here as quickly as you could. Well, I of course accept your offering, though shall be saving it for when our victory's achieved. {#Emph}This{#Prev}, however, you may be able to use sooner...

1.Text: {#Emph}Huh. {#Prev}Try as I might to consider each possibility, partaking of Nectar in the midst of this conflict that we're in is quite unthinkable. Still, it's something to look forward to.

2.Text: If it's something to look forward to, then it's a greater gift than I thought. The idea of a sip of Nectar while at peace... it does sound good.

1.Text: Your gesture is unnecessary. Warring mortals often make me offerings in hopes that I might guide them to victory. But you and I have a shared purpose, so I require no such incentives in our case.

2.Text: This is no incentive, merely a way of saying thank you. For accepting me, and recognizing what potential I may have to aid our family in a time of need.

1.Text: You honor me, and have my thanks. This Nectar, it's been to the Underworld and back... along with you. It'll take on a particularly complex flavor, I should think.

2.Text: If this bottle indeed traveled to the ends of the earth before returning home, then it's all the more suited to someone of your wisdom and experience. May you enjoy it once you lay down your arms.

1.Text: At this rate, we might someday have ourselves a feast to rival one arranged by Dionysus himself! Then let us fight with all our might to bring about such an enticing possibility.

2.Text: Here's to a future where you've time enough for feasting, not just military strategy. Though I'd not want to see you battle Dionysus, even when it comes to organizing feasts!

1.Text: You'd think being surrounded by family would mean being surrounded by like-minded folk, except... not many on Olympus think as I do. None, I daresay. Yet you... well, one difference is, I'd never deign give Nectar at a time like this.

2.Text: Lady Athena, I am honored to have joined your fight, and to have earned your blessings and your faith. I sometimes overlook the need to express my gratitude, and so rely on this Nectar to do it for me.

3.Text: Let it be said that we are goddesses of action, not words; and I accept your thoughtful, if oddly timed, offering. Though, let this be the last until our foes all lie in ruin.

1.Text: Of course.

I have something of a symbolic gift for you, Lady Athena, for I know Ambrosia shall flow in abundance on Olympus again soon. May this particular bottle contribute to the restoration, and remind you of our victories.

2.Text: I need no reminders of our victories, nor shall your generosity be forgotten during or after the restoration that inevitably is to come. What would we have done if not for you...?

3.Text: The Olympians have reigned for aeons, overcoming innumerable threats and setbacks. All this is but another; you would have figured out a way. {#Emph}Especially {#Prev}you.

4.Text: So adept at deflecting compliments even without my Boon. Then very well! Better to be modest than a braggart, I suppose. But you might aspire to be somewhere in between. Either that, or we should all be more like you.

1.Text: Let's all be who we are.
Lady Athena, by your leave... we have a mutual acquaintance I would ask about, because... well... do you recall the weaver Arachne?

2.Text: I seldom forget anything, Cousin. Especially not insolent mortals who see themselves as equals to the gods. Though she is not exactly mortal anymore. What of her?

3.Text: Well... she lives in Erebus now, near where I reside, and... she's so wretched about her appearance, which I understand is from a curse you wrought... doubtless entirely deserved, but... have mercy on her, Lady Athena. Please.

4.Text: So many mortals grovel to me all the time. But goddesses? And on behalf of mortals far too prideful to grovel for themselves? Cousin, do not waste my time with this.

1.Text: The mortal woman called Arachne. Have you any idea what she did? She fancied herself the greatest weaver in the world; superior even to me, if not the Fates themselves. Is it not our obligation, then, to remind mortals of their place?

2.Text: I... can't say I rightly know the answer to that, Lady Athena. Nor would I ever question your decision about her! I only ask if the term of her punishment could be less than eternal. She's humbled, and she's learned from her mistakes.

3.Text: Has she, now? In my experience mortals can be {#Emph}very {#Prev}slow to learn. And she was not punished as a lesson to {#Emph}her{#Prev}, but as a lesson to {#Emph}everyone else. {#Prev}I do not go back on my decisions, Melinoë. For I don't make them lightly.

1.Text: Your thoughts about Arachne are causing you distraction, which in turn is causing {#Emph}me {#Prev}distraction now. I would propose a means by which we could put this matter with her to rest.

2.Text: Truly? Please let me know what you have in mind, Lady Athena. Arachne is a friend, and if there's some way I could help her, I would. I already know the source of the curse...

3.Text: And so you need for me to let it lapse. And while you cannot compel me, perhaps Arachne can, if she is now as different as you say. You know my Gorgon Amulet? Ask if she would speak with me through it. If so, I may make an appearance.

1.Text: Lady Athena, I... I don't know what to say, except... I deeply regret the incident between you and Arachne. I was certain she sought your forgiveness, not an altercation.

2.Text: I am less surprised by the outcome, but then I knew Arachne from before. Perhaps she did {#Emph}mean {#Prev}to apologize, until the moment she saw me again and all her scorn came rushing back. Nonetheless, what's done is done.

3.Text: ...I understand. Though, if I may ask... what did she do to have incurred your judgment? I know a weaving contest was involved, but only from her side of the tale.

4.Text: Losing to some mortal was a humiliation I did not anticipate. Yet it was Arachne's arrogance that sparked my wrath, rather than any envy I had for her considerable talent. She had the nerve to call my work {#Emph}pedestrian.

5.Text: She insulted you... that was short-sighted, certainly, and as I understand she was quite young. Had she but known...

6.Text: This last time, she {#Emph}did {#Prev}know. Yet she insulted me again. We do not expect much from mortals; merely penitence. For those such as Arachne, the best we can do is make examples of them. Now I shall spare her not another word.

1.Text: My half-brother Ares must be having the time of his life, wherever he resides. He relishes a good protracted war... why would he work with us to put an end to it?

2.Text: Do you suspect betrayal? If Ares isn't here, and the war rages... perhaps he's stoking the conflict on the other side.

3.Text: The thought has certainly occurred to me, except... our enemy is no more interested in a war that lasts forever than we are. Whereas Ares wants only for the war to perpetuate, not for a victor to emerge.

4.Text: You know who else wants that is Eris. She's mentioned Ares before. You don't suppose they're working together?

5.Text: From what I know of Strife, she's not prone to alliances. Yet, I cannot rule out the possibility. She's been impeding you along your route... perhaps she'll let slip some detail.

1.Text: So Ares has decided to participate in our family activities after all. Ever willing to compromise! For if one everlasting war cannot be had, he'd settle for an outcome that ensures more wars are still to come.

2.Text: I know your views of war are not the same as his. But I will not decline his power on the basis of beliefs. Which means I'm willing to compromise, too... if doing so brings victory.

3.Text: Be careful with that line of thought, Cousin. Compromising to achieve consensus is one thing; but compromising on beliefs or principles... on {#Emph}ideals? {#Prev}Such reasoning is how wars often {#Emph}start{#Prev}, not merely end.

1.Text: I'm yet to be convinced that these Automatons we use in our defense are as dependable as can be. I've told Hephaestus I won't tolerate their quirks; nor should you.

2.Text: They are remarkable, but seem unable to fully distinguish your allies from your enemies. Perhaps Hephaestus can make improvements to their design.

3.Text: Yes, that's on a long list of requests we have for him. We'll have to decommission and repurpose any existing models for that effort anyhow... so if you destroy some here and there, it's for the best.

1.Text: Cousin, is it true that you reached the heart of your father's Underworld and vanquished the Titan Chronos there? His forces unexpectedly fell back, and I dared not trust my intuition as to why.

2.Text: I did prevail against him recently, yes. One night we shall dispose of him entirely, but for now, small victories shall have to suffice.

3.Text: Imperative victories are not small victories. Yet I fully understand the impulse never to grow complacent, and always to fight on.

1.Text: There's some strange spell at work on you, for you seem different than before. Much... more substantial. Whether a blessing or a curse, I can't immediately say.

2.Text: It's a blessing, or at least I think it is. The craft of Madame Circe the Enchantress, whom I encountered on my voyage here.

3.Text: Oh, her I do recall. She once created quite the predicament for a mortal seafarer whom I intended to protect, no one I think you'd know. I'd watch myself with her.

1.Text: There's some strange spell at work on you, for you seem different than before. Have you... shrunk down, Cousin? Whether a blessing or a curse, I can't immediately say.

2.Text: It's a blessing, or at least I think it is. The craft of Madame Circe the Enchantress, whom I encountered on my voyage here.

3.Text: Oh, her I do recall. She once created quite the predicament for a mortal seafarer whom I intended to protect, no one I think you'd know. I'd watch myself with her.

1.Text: You appear different than before. Another one of the enchantress Circe's unconventional blessings, then. Are you certain that she's aiding you, not... ridiculing you?

2.Text: Madame Circe would never use her transformation magick for ridicule. This is a powerful incantation... merely with certain side effects.

3.Text: Never use her magick for ridicule? That doesn't sound much like the Circe I recall. Perhaps she's learned to behave herself, though I am not convinced...

1.Text: You appear different than before. Another one of the enchantress Circe's unconventional blessings, then. Are you certain that she's aiding you, not... ridiculing you?

2.Text: Madame Circe would never use her transformation magick for ridicule. This is a powerful incantation... merely with certain side effects.

3.Text: Never use her magick for ridicule? That doesn't sound much like the Circe I recall. Perhaps she's learned to behave herself, though I am not convinced...

1.Text: My understanding was that your brother suffered from a certain ailment that inhibited his vitality if ever he attempted to venture out of the Underworld. Yet you apparently have no such limitation?

2.Text: I merely found the means to slow the effect, but I can feel it encroaching even now. If our foes aren't able to drive me to retreat, my ailment eventually shall.

3.Text: What can I say? You hide your troubles well, Melinoë. So yours is a race against time in more ways than one. I won't delay you any further then.

1.Text: I must say, Cousin... I've not seen such unity from our family in some time. Almost everybody stands together now against our foes. Though Dionysus, probably he's lying somewhere in a stupor.

2.Text: If Lord Dionysus hasn't taken up arms against the forces of Chronos, surely he has his reasons...

3.Text: Oh, he does. Why should he callus his hands, when he could laze about feasting? He's fortunate I've more important matters to consider than locating him.

1.Text: Well at least it isn't snowing here. I thought such devastation would be concentrated on Olympus, but it has spread all the way to Ephyra.

2.Text: The Titan's legions may have ransacked this city for symbolic reasons... raising their banners while destroying any monuments to the Underworld King and Queen.

3.Text: Ransacking requires no premeditation or strategic purpose, and the result of it is clear. But what I fail to see is how this helps persuade mortals to side with Titans over us.

1.Text: These must be the dark woods of Erebus, somewhere near your base of operations. I can see why they left such an impression on Artemis.

2.Text: Welcome, Lady Athena! Perhaps Artemis feels somewhat at home in woods of any sort, even ones haunted by Lost Souls denied their eternal rest.

3.Text: It's certainly a change from Mount Olympus. But I'm not here to survey the terrain, so quickly choose.

1.Text: The Three Fates themselves are gone, Hermes has said. Our situation grows that much more desperate, then. And yet... I never could depend on outside influence in my success; I trust you take no offense.

2.Text: No, I understand what you mean. Chronos feared some sort of Fated prophecy would do him in again, like when our fathers overthrew his rule. But if the Fates no longer are setting the course of what transpires... then we shall.

3.Text: We shall. For the goal of any strategy is to leave as little as possible to chance. We count only on those who prove themselves dependable, and above all, ourselves.

1.Text: {#Emph}Ungh... {#Prev}these Fields of Mourning have some similarity to sprawling plains upon the surface, but the air hangs very heavy here.

2.Text: Thank you for locating me even in such a place, Lady Athena. I wouldn't advise staying for long even if you could.

3.Text: And I wouldn't advise getting run through by my spear, yet at times it must be done. May your journey through this place take not a moment longer than it must.

1.Text: So Artemis discovered you within the mists of Erebus, under the tutelage of Hecate? Quite the tale. Would you care to elaborate?

2.Text: All I can say is Headmistress Hecate was under strict orders never to reveal me to anyone outside her inner circle. Not until our opportunity to strike at Chronos presented itself.

3.Text: Very well. I was never under the delusion that our side of the family and yours kept no secrets from each other. Likely it's for the best. But, my position does require a certain thoroughness and curiosity, you understand.

1.Text: My Stepmother Queen Hera's favor isn't easily earned. You should know it's she who first desired your assistance here. You have more than her Boon, but her faith; fragile as it is.

2.Text: And I am grateful for it, but... do you happen to know why? I don't know what Her Majesty the Queen could have seen in me, especially since we'd never even met.

3.Text: Perhaps it's that you represent a different course of action than the one we'd previously decided on, which came directly from my father your Lord Uncle Zeus. None of us like to be wrong about anything, but... we like victory more.

1.Text: You have perhaps encountered mighty Heracles along your route. He has surpassing strength and capability, but do report to me any suspicious actions on his part.

2.Text: I have encountered him, and seen him lay to waste droves of our foes, though he's not been keen on conversation. Which sorts of suspicious actions do you mean?

3.Text: Consorting with our foes, defying our will, anything of that sort. I have no real reason not to trust him, yet... I've come to trust you more.

1.Text: The mighty Heracles has remained silently obedient in all of this, expressing very little, which in turn tells me a lot. What's your assessment of him presently?

2.Text: {#Emph}Oh{#Prev}, I... well, he's exceptionally strong, true to his reputation, but besides that he... does not seem on the best of terms with the King and Queen.

3.Text: {#Emph}Hm. {#Prev}He must feel that he has more to lose by violating their will than bending to it, but... a warrior such as that... we would be wiser to ensure he's treated well.

1.Text: All of this warfare leaves us time for little else. I used to weave, you know. Great tapestries and more! May I have opportunity to take it up again once all this is behind us. And you, what else has occupied your time?

2.Text: I, well... I like to spar! Improving my acuity and strength. And practicing my craft. Matters of magick, the living, and the dead. How they're connected.

3.Text: I'm familiar with witchcraft, yes. Though, that all sounds like preparation for the matter you're now seeking to resolve! But I do realize it's not the time for flights of fancy, or even the discussion thereof.

1.Text: You bear the Amulet I gave to you. May it protect you and strike fear into the hearts of your enemies, whenever I am not around to do the same.

2.Text: Thank you, Lady Athena. The creature engraved on this... it's a Gorgon, isn't it? A guardian of some sort?

3.Text: Oh, not exactly, no. More of a cautionary reminder about what happens when we gods are openly defied. Don't lose your head out there, Cousin.

1.Text: You take me to the strangest places with that Gorgon Amulet, Cousin. I'm pleased you've gained such use from it.

2.Text: I'm certain you're aware that your blessings are extraordinarily valuable, Lady Athena. As long as my repeated summons haven't been too inconvenient.

3.Text: When it is inconvenient, I do not show up. Then let us keep charting this strange path together, not alone!

1.Text: You got me thinking about mortalkind of late. I, too, have taken a personal interest in mortals and their plights. Many times. Especially in those who rise above their station. And I wish to honor their worship of the other gods and me.

2.Text: Yet you said before that it's our obligation to remind them of their place... that they are ultimately powerless against us.

3.Text: Yes, for they outnumber us greatly, and many grow resourceful and independent. Some do not think they need us, but they do. Both in life and in death, as your father would attest. Best not become {#Emph}too {#Prev}attached to any of them.

1.Text: You have been very well prepared... outfitted with excellent equipment, knowledgeable of the twists and turns through our mountain, not to mention even getting there. Whoever plotted your course is good at it.

2.Text: Thank you, Lady Athena. We had to know what we were getting ourselves into given the precarity of the situation, so we planned as best we could.

3.Text: Indeed. Though I find such strategic insight is less likely to come from a collective {#Emph}we {#Prev}than from a single, sound mind. Nobody's business but your own, of course.

1.Text: The depths of Oceanus... I have often soared or sailed over these waters, but not often seen them from within. So this is how you circumvent Elysium.

2.Text: An indirect route to the lowest reaches, yes. Perhaps you'll frighten off some of the fishlike horrors.

3.Text: Such base creatures have little capacity for fear, but we shall teach them of it what we can.

1.Text: It almost looks as though you're having to contend with the invaders on your own, Lady Athena. There's a lot of mountain to cover, with too few allies...

2.Text: Well, we have {#Emph}you{#Prev}, Cousin. As for our {#Emph}other {#Prev}allies... we as a family are loath to beg assistance, or for anything. To all our followers and compatriots, our message has been clear: We have this matter well under control.

3.Text: Is that the truth of it, or merely posturing, if you'll pardon my bluntness? You are clearly being overrun.

4.Text: On the contrary, our Automatons have quite effectively held many of our enemies at bay. And you and I can make a significant difference as well, if we don't dally.

1.Text: My father's Palace is now closed for retrofitting, probably much like what's underway in {#Emph}your {#Prev}father's realm... leaving you with nowhere to rest after a hard night's work.

2.Text: It's all right, Lady Athena. I mustn't stay here longer than I have to, and recover far more swiftly where I'm from.

3.Text: You fight as though you're unencumbered, but I know the surface weighs on you. It is impressive how you've learned to suppress this Fate-wrought weakness in your blood.

1.Text: After we settled certain troubles with your brother's situation at home, your mother Persephone, she would regularly return to Olympus for part of each year. I should have trusted my instincts when one day she failed to show...

2.Text: Presumably when Chronos struck. Wouldn't her sudden disappearance have been cause for considerable alarm?

3.Text: You'd think. However, we knew your mother was with child, and our conclusion was that your new family wanted privacy. So we waited patiently, not realizing it as Chronos gained his foothold. A grave miscalculation on my part...

4.Text: Your father and mine first fought and vanquished Chronos long before either of us was born. You couldn't have expected the Titan Lord to suddenly return.

5.Text: Yet if I'm to be the strategist upon Olympus then I have to consider each possibility, however unlikely, that can threaten our peace. At any rate, a lesson harshly learned...

1.Text: Beware ahead. The Titan Prometheus is able to elude me, knowing that I'm focused on his vanguard forces. But he'll have no choice but to confront you if you press on.

2.Text: He's the Titan of Foresight. He knows exactly what we're planning, doesn't he? And can retaliate accordingly.

3.Text: He knows what is to come to some extent, yes. But he can only see outcomes, not read minds. And just because he knows you're coming doesn't mean he can stop you.

1.Text: Have you confronted Prometheus before? You mentioned he's been able to elude you. Perhaps he knows he'd stand no chance against you if you fought.

2.Text: I knew Prometheus prior to all this. I suppose our tendencies toward matters of the mind connected us. You know that he stole the gift of fire for mortalkind. Well... he also gave them reason, from me. Some of them, anyway.

3.Text: I shudder to think what mortals must have been like before they had any reason. Although perhaps Prometheus ought to have kept some reason for himself.

4.Text: Perhaps he thinks he did, or has as much as he requires. Unfortunately, reason tends to be in lesser abundance than most would dare to admit.

1.Text: Even if you're thwarted by the Titan Prometheus, it is a benefit to our war effort. For if he's having to confront you, then he's unable to cause his mayhem elsewhere.

2.Text: That is of little consolation to me, Lady Athena. This is not his first crime against Olympus and our family; thus his punishment is to be even more severe.

3.Text: Do not concern yourself with that. His prior punishment inspired this still-greater transgression, rather than remorse for his past deeds. For the moment, our strategy merely requires that he not stand in our way.

1.Text: It's always good to see you, Lady Athena. You truly are relentless in this continued effort.

2.Text: Hardly an effort at this point, but good to see you likewise, Cousin. These meetings provide a welcome change from having to dispose of our enemies with extreme prejudice.

1.Text: The Moon herself assists you, that I know. We often underestimate her here, believing all she does is faintly light the sky. But I know there is more to her than that.

2.Text: Selene may be a Titaness but she's an ally to us through and through. She upholds Night's will, as do I.

3.Text: Nyx's will is none of my concern, Cousin. But apparently it's yours, and Nyx has likewise been an ally to Olympus in the past. If you trust Selene's involvement, that is enough.

1.Text: This night is darker than so many others of late, and our foes appear emboldened. Some new trick of Chronos, or... perhaps merely my imagination from fighting for so long.

2.Text: It isn't your imagination but the will of Night herself, Lady Athena. And though the effect may seem to our detriment for now, we shall grow stronger for it, I assure you.

3.Text: Such assurances mean little to me typically, Cousin. But you know more about the darkness than I do. If this truly is the will of Night, and not the work of our enemy, then good.

1.Text: Such horrors have befallen our proud summit. This is intolerable... I ask myself how I might have prevented it.

2.Text: I would have no good answer, Lady Athena. Olympus is facing a coordinated attack on multiple fronts, from the air, earth, and sea. Your Automatons can only do so much.

3.Text: But we can {#Emph}always {#Prev}do more even if those mindless machines cannot. We could have done more! For now, though... we had best focus on the resolution, not the cause.

1.Text: So then it's true, what Chronos said... these possibilities that Typhon could have remained. Or perhaps the Gorgon Amulet is letting me share your hallucinations now.

2.Text: It all seems real enough to me... especially having retraced my path up to this point. But we can stop this here just as we did before.

3.Text: Then that is what we shall do. There is no reason to change strategies as long as they keep yielding good results.

1.Text: Have you felt the growing tremors during your approach, Cousin? I don't care for them at all. Lord Uncle Poseidon at first acted as though they were his doing, but not even he seems to know the source...

2.Text: In the Underworld, we experience tremors all the time, for the Earth is all around us, living and breathing. But I'm surprised such shaking could be felt all the way up here...

3.Text: Perhaps because it's more than the Earth living and breathing. Our enemy is behind this, I am certain of it.

1.Text: I must apologize about your confrontation with the particularly large and dangerous Automaton called Talos. It detects traces of the Underworld on you, and, well...

2.Text: It's a magnificent creation, and Lord Hephaestus should be proud... though, the methods by which his Automatons detect threats could probably use a comprehensive rework.

3.Text: I shall be certain to relay the suggestion. Unfortunately Lord Hephaestus prioritized a self-repairing system in Talos over threat-detection, so it may continue to be an issue for now.

1.Text: All this gold... what has become of Tartarus? The Titan Chronos rendered it almost entirely unrecognizable...

2.Text: Perhaps when next I use the Gorgon Amulet to summon you here, you could ask him yourself, Lady Athena.

3.Text: Oh, would that I could and the Amulet were even stronger. But all strategies have limitations. My blessing rather than my presence shall have to do as you approach your goal.

1.Text: This sailing-vessel's rotting deck... we are amid the Titan's fleet in Lord Uncle Poseidon's Rift. You use such means to reach our mountain every night?

2.Text: Well... some nights I go to the Underworld instead, but otherwise, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, yes. I've not had much success learning to fly or shift between the realms.

3.Text: I laud your ingenuity... you, or whoever plotted such a course, that turns the enemy's advance to an advantage.

1.Text: You are a welcome sight, Melinoë, for it has been some nights since last we met upon the battlefield like this. How fares the war beneath the Earth?

2.Text: It rages on. Night after night the Titan's legions regroup, while he asserts that he cannot be stopped. But I am working on disproving that. And what news here?

3.Text: The mountain stands, as you can see, and that is what matters. Perhaps your presence and a corresponding shift in strategy shall lead us to the breakthrough that we need.

1.Text: It has been longer than I'd like, Cousin! Our enemies abound, and lately I've dealt with more than my share.

2.Text: Apologies, Lady Athena. Matters drew my attention from Olympus, though I was confident you and the others would hold fast while I was away.

3.Text: And hold fast we did. But when you're here, I find we can go beyond merely defending, and properly fight back.

1.Text: You've seen what plagues us at the summit, haven't you? The source of all the tremors... almost as though the mountain itself quakes with fear. We need a plan...

2.Text: The gods have stood against Typhon before. Wasn't it a well-placed thunderbolt from Zeus that did him in?

3.Text: Tales of valor and {#Emph}deeds {#Prev}of valor are not always one and the same. Then let us lure this Typhon toward the summit, where our strength combined with yours is the best opportunity we have... and please take care, Cousin.

1.Text: I have been called a savior many times, and take some pleasure in overturning near-hopeless situations. But recently, it was my own hope that faltered... until {#Emph}you {#Prev}restored it. The Father of All Monsters is truly gone.

2.Text: Olympus belongs to the gods... Typhon's destruction was a necessity. I may have been the one to deliver him to the void, but the doing of it took our combined strength.

3.Text: You chthonic gods and your modesty. Be {#Emph}proud{#Prev}, Cousin! You have achieved a glorious result, for which we all are thankful. I knew I {#Emph}had {#Prev}to trust you. But I also felt I should.

1.Text: Thank the Fates that you eluded Typhon's fury. And you created enough of a diversion that we were able to fortify our defenses and keep that monstrosity at bay, for now.

2.Text: But he'll be back. Have you discovered any weaknesses of note? I'd rather do more than distract him.

3.Text: A being of that size will not have many weaknesses... although no creature likes to be jabbed in the eyes; and Typhon has a great many of them, for better or worse. And if we muster all our powers... perhaps we can drive him back.

1.Text: Cousin, after much consideration, I admit the best plan that I have for stopping Typhon at this point... is to rely on {#Emph}you. {#Prev}The next best alternative available would be most dire.

2.Text: Lord Uncle Zeus alluded to some force that could potentially defeat that monster, but bring great harm to Olympus in the process... is that the alternative you mean?

3.Text: It is. My energies, as you can see, are focused on repelling our enemy's forces here. But it seems I shall also have to dissuade my father from taking a catastrophic course, if but to buy you time. I'm counting on you... we all are.

1.Text: We were able to repel that monstrous Typhon thanks to your aid! So it {#Emph}can {#Prev}be done! Only the contemptible thing soon recovered and commenced his climb once more...

2.Text: There has to be a way to vanquish Typhon utterly, not just slow him down. But if slowing him's the best result we can achieve for now... so be it.

3.Text: The so-called {#Emph}Father of All Monsters... {#Prev}I heard the tales many times of course, but {#Emph}seeing {#Prev}him... I felt my courage almost falter; which was more frightening even than the thing itself...

1.Text: That Typhon seems only to grow angrier each time we withstand his rage. A clever ploy for Chronos to set such a thing on us... keeping us occupied, while he plots his next move.

2.Text: Whether clever or reckless, I'm not yet convinced. Chronos is counting on Typhon turning all his violence against Olympus, but after that...? Not even {#Emph}he {#Prev}can control such an abomination.

3.Text: Perhaps Chronos means to seal the monster away once we are no longer a threat. At any rate, we don't intend to let any such outcome transpire.

1.Text: First you vanquished Chronos in your father's realm, then in turn you toppled Typhon from our mountain's heights. I must admit, I underestimated you when first we met.

2.Text: I've trained my entire life for this eventuality, Lady Athena. It's what should be expected of me, and besides... our war isn't over yet.

3.Text: You trained with Hecate to vanquish Chronos, that I know. But Typhon was never part of your practice routine. Yet I, too, dislike compliments especially when, to your point, our war is not yet won.

1.Text: You bear the Arms of Night. I suspected it when we first met but now my doubt is gone. Should the Underworld be imperiled, those weapons are to be the last resort, fine. But they seem well outside their jurisdiction here.

2.Text: The peril that the Underworld faces evidently spread even to this mountain. For my part, the Nocturnal Arms have proven equally dependable above the surface and below.

3.Text: Make certain that you keep their power well in check, as well as their hunger. I much prefer my weapons not to have intentions of their own, but can't deny their potency.

1.Text: How strange it is to meet you face-to-face. Your brother Zagreus I spoke to many times, though by Boon all but once. You must know he had his struggles at home. Now it seems your side of the family is repaying us for back then.

2.Text: If there's a debt to be repaid then I am unaware, Lady Athena. I'm here because our family is in peril, my side and yours.

3.Text: Of course, and it wasn't my intent to suggest otherwise. I'm merely reflecting on the change of circumstance. Well then, one Boon deserves another.

1.Text: You didn't remind me of Zagreus at first but I do see some of it now. I've not had occasion to resume Boon messages to him, or for that matter you. I trust he's well?

2.Text: He seems to be in good spirits, yes. Even though we met just recently, I feel as though I've known him for a while. How did the two of you first come into contact anyhow?

3.Text: The goddess Nyx is how. A long tale for another time but I thought she was his mother at first. Each of us was raised without a mother, come to think! Regards to all your kin.

1.Text: You should know, my father your Lord Uncle Zeus is somewhat skeptical of your ability to turn the outcome of the war here in our favor. He believes we should be able to fend for ourselves; and I don't disagree.

2.Text: Lady Athena, are we supposed to stand united as a family or aren't we? This isn't the time to be prideful.

3.Text: With that, I don't disagree either. Nevertheless, our family seems incapable of standing united for long. If we could... this war never would have started.

1.Text: I shall ensure this area remains secure for now; make your advance!
Continue your ascent, as I shall keep what passes for the Titan's armies occupied.
They never seem to learn, do they? But neither do they ever seem to stop.
I trust that our defenses have not proven too much of a hindrance to you here.
When our family stands united, there's no hardship that we cannot overcome.
I've wrath to spare for all those you shall confront on your way to the summit.
Make haste toward the Palace, Cousin, and my blessing be with you.
Another victory is within reach; go take it, and I'll cover you as you proceed.
Battle rages all around us still, Melinoë. Then let us finish what our enemies began.
This mountain stronghold of ours shall never fall, try as the Titan might.
Climb forth, Cousin, and may your foothold never falter on the way.
Go quickly but with care; my father and the rest await you at the summit.
I'm grateful that you're back, so that the next stage of our plan can now unfold.
You're all the reinforcements we require, and I'm ever-grateful that you're here.
Would that we could fight together, yet we accomplish more going our separate ways.
Our foes swarm at us like insects, and we shall deal with them as such.
I knew that I could count on you to be here tonight precisely at this time.
Many such victories are still to come before our war is finally ended.
It is not enough merely to vanquish our enemies; let us make an example of them.
The peak of Olympus awaits; go, and I'll ensure you need not watch your back.
I know you've scores to settle in the Underworld, so thank you for being here.
Your skill alone has brought you to this point, although perhaps I may assist.
Let our enemies rue the moment they deigned to stand against we gods.
It is as though the Moon herself directed me to your position here tonight.
Our family has endured for aeons; this shall pass, as does all else.
All those who dare oppose us or our rightful rule shall be given no quarter.
Proceed immediately to the Palace and I'll cover you, Melinoë.
What use is a good strategy without the necessary skill to see it through?
The Titan's forces know nothing of fear, but I trust that they can still be taught.
May the Boon I now bestow provide a difference in the battles yet to come.
Choose swiftly, Cousin, as there's another pack of uninvited guests I'd better intercept.
Well this is certainly a change of scenery from Mount Olympus, isn't it?
If ever I grow weary of Olympus, one look at {#Emph}this {#Prev}place shall make me long for it again.
Your victory last night predicts another soon to come, especially now that I'm here.
Our enemies ought to have learned they stand no chance against us anymore.
The air hangs heavy, and our enemies are coursing with new strength. Let us beware.
Let no trace remain of the Father of All Monsters, for all the harm that he has wrought.
If this is how we shall assert our dominance for ages hence, then so be it.
Would that I could be in several places all at once, but I chose a good one here.
Our family is as close to perfect as can be, but let us strive to become greater still.
Pleased to see a friendly face. Fending off the Titan's legions can be solitary work.
Each such battle is nothing; yet we must pace ourselves for a protracted fight.
You surely could have handled all those wretches well enough on your own.
No need to trade extensive pleasantries. Let's each of us remain on task.
I had anticipated that you'd soon return. I trust the Underworld work proceeded well.
I cannot reach your Underworld easily or for long, but know you'll keep it well under control.
Do not forget about my Amulet should you have need of me elsewhere, Cousin.
May all those who threaten our divine rule suffer tenfold for their arrogance.
The noble Princess of the Dead, at last! I am your cousin Athena, and proud to welcome you to Olympus. Yet I could be prouder, as this wasn't always such a miserable place.

2.Text: Hail, Lady Athena, and well met! Please call me Melinoë. Now where can I direct my wrath, that we may liberate your mountain stronghold and see its glory all restored?

3.Text: Well met indeed, Melinoë. The wretched Titan's armies have infiltrated our most sacred grounds. On them, your wrath may be well-spent; especially as you rise toward the summit, where most of our family now takes refuge.

4.Text: The Palace of Zeus. And what of you, why aren't the others out here fighting by your side?

5.Text: Because that is precisely what our strategy requires, for they aided your arrival, did they not? Now, let us go our separate ways, and may my blessing aid in your ascent.

1.Text: I've something here for you, Cousin. Seeing as you remain instrumental to our mountain's ongoing defense.

2.Text: I'm honored, Lady Athena. A family such as ours ought to stand together during times of need. I wish to do my part.

3.Text: You have impressed not only me but all our kin; most of them, I should say. And for that, I bestow my greatest power. May it soon bring about still greater victories.

1.Text: You're injured, Cousin... though I shouldn't be so surprised. It is a grueling climb to reach this point, and you traversed the Rift of Thessaly as well. Are you all right?

2.Text: I can press on in this state, Lady Athena. Though whether I've the strength to surpass Prometheus, let alone what awaits beyond... that I can't guarantee.

3.Text: In war there are no guarantees save bloodshed, as Ares surely would attest, wherever he may be rejoicing. Now let's get you back to proper fighting shape.

1.Text: ...I had considered how we would proceed if by some chance the Three Fates were never found. What I did not anticipate was that they {#Emph}would {#Prev}be found, yet still take leave of their responsibilities... so I am told.

2.Text: They've been weaving for aeons, and perhaps felt weary or even underappreciated. That, or they liked what they saw while their weavings were on hold. They did give us a big new prophecy as a sort of parting gift.

3.Text: A prophecy about another age, that we gods shall relinquish our dominion to mortals... it's difficult to believe. But then, these things never unfold precisely as they sound.

4.Text: No... and for that matter, I couldn't tell whether the Fates were angry, or disappointed, or anything like that... on the contrary, they seemed enthusiastic.

5.Text: They are weavers, whose tapestries reveal the vast and complicated tale of history. Perhaps they seek merely to entertain, and we are but characters they have to work with.

1.Text: So many battles have been fought and many yet remain. But we goddesses are tireless. You can count on me for as long as you choose to press on.

2.Text: Choose to press on... at times I feel obligated, Lady Athena. The possibilities of Typhon and Chronos... who shall stop them if not us?

3.Text: A proper strategy requires taking every reasonable precaution, but can also be adapted should the need arise. Let us account for as many possibilities as we see fit, but never to the detriment of other matters of concern.

1.Text: We have achieved a monumental victory, Cousin. Although the annihilation of one's enemies can be a serviceable outcome in war, surrender often is preferred. I trust the others have expressed their gratitude?

2.Text: Yes, of course. And congratulations to you all, Lady Athena. My only regret is that this siege cannot immediately cease, given what's left to be done.

3.Text: Abandon that regret, for the rabble that still plagues Olympus is nothing. As for Prometheus, though I am skeptical about his role in this new strategy, I have persuaded Father to go along with it, for now...

1.Text: Now you are to confront these traces of our great foes, both at the summit and in Tartarus... re-creating the path that got you there, as though the possibilities need to align...?

2.Text: That's how our grandfather explains it, more or less. Almost like we're circumventing outcomes in which we might otherwise have failed for one reason or another.

3.Text: There ought to be very few such outcomes then. For we do not fail; merely take the necessary time to succeed.

1.Text: I'm pleased to know your family in the Underworld is safe, as well as Nyx and those who served the House of Hades. For all our troubles here, at least we were not divided... more than usual.

2.Text: Chronos took his wrath out on my father, but my mother and the rest were imprisoned in an instant... frozen in time. They awakened with no knowledge of this whole ordeal.

3.Text: Perhaps they are the most fortunate ones in all this. Though we shall have to be patient with their many questions.

1.Text: You honor me, my lady.

2.Text: Glory to Olympus!
