1.Text: I'm most grateful... and wish I could stay for the festivities.
I... don't wish to be just some ungrateful guest. I know you have your customs here, and I have studied them. So, please! For all your cheer and generosity!

2.Text: Whoa, this is Nectar, it's the real thing, we could use every drop that we can get! Then here is something for my most distinguished guests, of which I have decided {#Emph}you are one!

1.Text: Hey, {#Emph}nice{#Prev}, more Nectar always good to have around in case the wine runs out, not that it ever does or ever will! Now, what exactly do we toast to next?

2.Text: To emerging from peril unscathed? Or whatever you decide. I know maintaining high morale is paramount, especially with the mountain under siege.

1.Text: Cheers!
Cheers.

Hey, sure, I'll take that Nectar off your hands! As this here's {#Emph}just {#Prev}the place to put it to its proper use. But don't you get all sad and sappy with me, you're at a {#Emph}feast{#Prev}, not at a wake!

2.Text: I must admit, I'm unable to cast aside my fears and worries quite like you, Dionysus. It's little wonder mortals make so many offerings in your name... as now do I.

1.Text: Now that's the spirit, giving back to the community, I {#Emph}like {#Prev}it, yeah? After all, you know I can't make cheer and revelry for everyone all by myself, don't you? Though between us, I still can make an {#Emph}awful {#Prev}lot.

2.Text: Such cheer and revelry that you've created, seemingly out of thin air... and during such a time. Well, if this truly is to be a never-ending feast, then you'll need plenty of supplies!

1.Text: Hey this is {#Emph}great{#Prev}, there's not an entrance fee or anything, but tips are always welcome as our Nectar's running {#Emph}dangerously low. {#Prev}Got any more to spare?

2.Text: Oh, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, looks to me as if you've all had quite enough for now. But if I happen on a surplus... I'll bring more.

1.Text: You better, {#Emph}hahahaha!
All right, now that's exactly what we need, and ought to last till, what, tomorrow night at least? You've got my thanks and more, Mel baby! Who's your supplier, might I ask?

2.Text: I've no single Nectar source I rely on; I know a Broker who tends to have some, and at other times I find a bottle here and there. Has it truly been that difficult to find?

3.Text: Oh this stuff's not impossible to get most of the time, we just go through a lot is all! And now my guests are pining for Ambrosia more and more. Happen to have a box of that?

1.Text: A box? You mean a bottle.
A {#Emph}box {#Prev}of bottles! {#Emph}Good {#Prev}ones!
Here you are, then, Dionysus! One box of good bottles of Ambrosia. May this help keep things festive for your guests for quite some time... at least till next I happen to stop in...

2.Text: Mel, {#Emph}baby{#Prev}, I could {#Emph}kiss {#Prev}you, did you really bring all this for {#Emph}us?! {#Prev}This is exactly what we needed, I mean... how'd you even {#Emph}know? {#Prev}Can you read minds?

3.Text: ...You previously asked if I had access to Ambrosia, but... I cannot yet read minds most of the time. That is a very advanced skill.

4.Text: Oh come {#Emph}on {#Prev}you can probably read everything that's going on in {#Emph}mine! {#Prev}And mostly you'll be reading gratitude. I thought you were a little stiff at first but you're all right!

1.Text: That means a lot coming from you.
...Say what?

Say, any leads on finding us a box of good bottles of Ambrosia yet or what? We're down to our {#Emph}emergency ration {#Prev}here, making it {#Emph}last. {#Prev}I'm trying to keep everybody {#Emph}calm!

2.Text: I've not encountered such a box, and am uncertain how to best distinguish a good bottle from another. I'd no idea that Ambrosia could go bad...

3.Text: Well then, I'll let you in on a little secret, baby...! Just as soon as I remember what it was... {#Emph}haha{#Prev}, all this shaking lately, I can't even {#Emph}think! Erm{#Prev}, you want one of {#Emph}these?

1.Text: Oh hey! The mountain finally stopped shaking for a bit and I remembered what I wanted you to know! A {#Emph}box of bottles of Ambrosia{#Prev}, that's just four of them at once. Technical term!

2.Text: So you don't just want {#Emph}one {#Prev}bottle of Ambrosia but {#Emph}four{#Prev}, and you don't want me to, say, give one bottle at a time...

3.Text: Come on look, how many {#Emph}guests {#Prev}I have... no single bottle's going to do! But now you know what we need to survive. I'll be counting on you, Mel baby!

1.Text: Oh you should have seen it, baby, the Ambrosia that you brought, it kicked things up like you would not {#Emph}believe!

2.Text: I can imagine! Though things don't seem that different than before. Have you depleted the entire box already?

3.Text: {#Emph}No! {#Prev}I mean... not really! I mean, maybe. But I have got a lead on a reserve so vast that we won't need donations anymore. And for {#Emph}you{#Prev}, I've got a little something extra {#Emph}here.

1.Text: Hey you didn't tell Apollo anything about what's going on in here, did you? Because I, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, I have not sent him an invite yet. I know he's busy wanting to be left alone!

2.Text: Lord Apollo has been gracious to support me with his Boons, but no, I've not informed him or any of your relatives about your feasting. That's your business not mine.

3.Text: {#Emph}Whew{#Prev}, cheers! He likes to keep things squeaky clean, you know, but I prefer it any other way! Something about you made me think of him but probably I'm just out of my mind!

1.Text: Have you run into any trouble with all the Automatons supposedly defending your domain? They attack me indiscriminately from your foes.

2.Text: Maybe they think you're too uptight! Come on Mel baby, you don't need to worry about us! I've got my special ways, which not even the works of Lord Hephaestus can resist.

3.Text: Your special ways... so then you know a means to bypass their threat detection. Can you show me how?

4.Text: Oh I can show you {#Emph}lots {#Prev}of things. Those clankers you're still on about, they're just like family! Sure, they fight sometimes, but they mean well. Just stay out of their way, yeah?

1.Text: {#Emph}Hey, {#Prev}little kitten, {#Emph}meooow, hahaha! {#Prev}And hey to {#Emph}you{#Prev}, Mel baby! So how about an introduction to your feline companion, yeah?

2.Text: Oh, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, this is Toula, and we keep each other safe. And fear not, for I'll be watching her closely, lest she help herself to all the nourishment about.

3.Text: No need for that, we've plenty here to go around, even with {#Emph}lots {#Prev}of different appetites! We're all just a bunch of animals here so {#Emph}yours {#Prev}are {#Emph}more {#Prev}than welcome to join the pack!

1.Text: Hey you look, {#Emph}ah{#Prev}, I mean, {#Emph}wow. {#Prev}Did you grow bigger, and I mean that purely as a compliment... or did I grow smaller, or... {#Emph}eugh{#Prev}, my head...

2.Text: Oh, you mean... my unusually greater height! It's due to a fleeting bit of magick from my companion, the enchantress called Circe. So the effect is rather noticeable, then?

3.Text: I mean, {#Emph}yeah! {#Prev}Circe, huh, I know that name! Sounds like she knows a trick or two! Maybe she'll get an invite to the next one of {#Emph}these!

1.Text: Hey you look, {#Emph}erm... {#Prev}did you shrink down or something, or... did I grow bigger all of a sudden, or... {#Emph}oh{#Prev}, my head...

2.Text: Oh, right... a reminder about my temporarily reduced stature. It's due to a bit of magick from my companion, the enchantress Circe. So the effect is rather noticeable, then?

3.Text: I mean, {#Emph}yeah! {#Prev}Circe, huh, I know that name! Sounds like she knows a trick or two! Maybe she'll get an invite to the next one of {#Emph}these!

1.Text: Hey look at you, Mel baby, you are {#Emph}huge! {#Prev}I {#Emph}like {#Prev}it! Once knew some Amazons about your size, they were a {#Emph}real {#Prev}handful, if you know what I mean!

2.Text: I think I do know, yes, now that you've helpfully reminded me how I have temporarily increased in size. It offers me a tactical advantage for the night.

3.Text: Oh I am positively sure it does! And if my Amazonian companions were here they would wholeheartedly agree. And probably demand you wrestle them.

1.Text: {#Emph}Aw{#Prev}, look how {#Emph}little {#Prev}you are, baby! {#Emph}Ahem {#Prev}that's sounding a bit rude, when I say {#Emph}baby {#Prev}you know I don't mean it like {#Emph}that!

2.Text: That's quite all right. I know my reduced stature may be off-putting. All part of the advantage it affords.

3.Text: Well I like 'em in every shape and size, it isn't all the same, it's all {#Emph}different! {#Prev}Small? Cool. Bigger? {#Emph}Great! {#Prev}I'm all about variety!

1.Text: {#Emph}Heeey{#Prev}, look who decided to reconsider coming to our little gathering! Welcome back, Mel baby, now go on, you grab yourself a cup and mingle with the crowd!

2.Text: As tempting as that sounds, Lord Dionysus, unfortunately I don't think I can. There are various perils beyond, and your fellow Olympians can only do so much to hold them off.

3.Text: And I feel bad for them, really! Almighty gods with limitless power having to fend for themselves. Good thing I can drown my sorrows here, and guess what? So can you!

1.Text: You really are just passing through? Look at all these temptations in every form! The liquid kind, the sumptuous kind, {#Emph}mm! {#Prev}But you're unmoved and undeterred?

2.Text: Look, I would truly love to stay. Enjoy a beverage and a bite... speak with all these doubtless-interesting guests... but I can't. Don't you understand? Your mountain is burning!

3.Text: Well if it's burning, baby, let it burn, I say! But I don't want to argue anymore, I mean, it's just another form of fighting, yeah? So you go do your thing, and I'll do mine!

1.Text: Lord Dionysus, just how long have you been feasting, anyhow? Here in this spot, I mean. Night after night, you're going at it like there's no tomorrow.

2.Text: Mel baby, just call me Dionysus if you please, the Lord thing doesn't suit me, yeah? As for how long we've carried on like this, I've no idea! A while probably. Might be a new record! {#Emph}Heh. {#Prev}Sure you don't want to join?

1.Text: What if you couldn't feast any longer? Imagine something so dire that it forced you to put a stop to this way of life. Brought ruin to everything you hold dear!

2.Text: I know what you're trying to do, baby, and it isn't going to work. I've tuned out {#Emph}every {#Prev}bit of negativity, including yours! And since I'm a good host, I'm {#Emph}still {#Prev}going to give you {#Emph}this.

1.Text: What's the occasion for the feasting, anyway? I fail to see what cause there is to celebrate right now.

2.Text: Don't you get it, baby? Every moment that we live and breathe is more than cause enough! Maybe you're into feeling bad, I don't know, but me? I'm into feeling {#Emph}good!

1.Text: Hey glad you could make it! I know there's a lot going on, but what's it all for if you can't kick back once in a while, yeah? So {#Emph}ease up {#Prev}a bit, you're {#Emph}here!

2.Text: I'm just passing through. Though, I truly appreciate your hospitality. Perhaps if and when all this is finally resolved, I can kick back, as you say.

3.Text: Oh I'll hold you to that, if I can remember you said it! For now though cheers to your success and all, and may your warring wrap up peaceably and soon!

1.Text: What's that with you, some sort of {#Emph}frog? {#Prev}Well sure, since frogs and me, we go way back! The only rule is there's no swimming in the spring or guests might get a little {#Emph}eugh!

2.Text: That's Frinos, and don't worry, not that you ever do. He won't disturb the peace, and avoids most others anyway. Thank you for permitting him here... and me, for that matter.

3.Text: Oh absolutely, it's the sort of feast where if you can get in at all, it means you're probably all right! Your frog there too, long as he doesn't sing! He doesn't sing, does he...?

1.Text: Does mighty Heracles ever stop by? He seems to do much of the heavy lifting out on the front lines and probably could use the break... though might bring down the mood.

2.Text: Oh believe me I have invited him don't know {#Emph}how {#Prev}many times but he won't {#Emph}budge{#Prev}, big man like that, I mean it figures, yeah? He's all obsessed with {#Emph}laboring away{#Prev}, won't cut loose even for a bit! Though maybe he'll listen to you...

3.Text: What, to join you for a drink and a splash in the hot springs? Why would Heracles possibly listen to {#Emph}me {#Prev}if your own powers of persuasion haven't been sufficient?

4.Text: Cause you're a {#Emph}girl{#Prev}, baby! You've got the voice, and the thing you do with your hair, the whole {#Emph}I'm-so-innocent {#Prev}act, it's enough to drive somebody wild! So {#Emph}ask {#Prev}him, yeah?

1.Text: Old Heracles decided to stop by, you see him there?! He's like a big old ox! Hop in the bath with him, go on, I want to see you try! Unless you did already and I missed it, {#Emph}eugh...

Mel, baby, I {#Emph}insist {#Prev}you introduce me to your dog there {#Emph}right {#Prev}away! I've not seen such a {#Emph}gorgeous {#Prev}breed since last I traveled west! I used to travel all around, you know.

2.Text: Dionysus, please meet Hecuba, who's in my care for now, and always on her best behavior as you'll see. Your journeys must have been amazing... seeing the world...

3.Text: Oh that they were but now I'm here where it's amazing too! Things never stay the same for very long, got to enjoy them while they last. Nothing lasts forever! Except us!

1.Text: That Fig Leaf that you're carrying... it's from my {#Emph}private wardrobe! {#Prev}So how come you have it and not me? What, did I just hand it over as a gift?

2.Text: You did exactly that, yes. I offered you a bottle of Nectar, and you gave me this Leaf in exchange. Don't you recall?

3.Text: Don't I recall... {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, sometimes! But not always, not so much of late! Well if past-me thought he should give you such a thing, he must have had a real good feeling for you, yeah?

1.Text: Quite an impressive cat beside you there. How did you manage to domesticate her? I thought such creatures tended to roam free.

2.Text: {#Emph}Domesticate {#Prev}her, Mel baby, you ought to know that Maena here, she is as {#Emph}wild {#Prev}as they come! And believe me I have known a {#Emph}lot {#Prev}of leopards in my time!

1.Text: You're not from around here, so how fare the mortals as of late? You've surely seen a few of them along your path. It's been a little while since I heard from them!

2.Text: They've been better! Most probably are praying to our family for peace, since Chronos flung open the Underworld's gates, leaving the dead to roam the land.

3.Text: Which means that mortals get to spend more time with long-lost relatives of theirs! Come on, stay {#Emph}positive{#Prev}, Mel baby! That's how mortals get by! It'll be all right!

1.Text: Not told my Dad about this little gathering of ours, have you? Because we wouldn't want to have to pack it up and find some other secret spot. It's perfect here!

2.Text: I think Lord Zeus has far more urgent matters to consider than your never-ending feast, which I daresay would be even better if the legions of Chronos weren't about. The rest of the Olympians don't even know that this is going on?

3.Text: Right you are, baby! For this is an {#Emph}exclusive {#Prev}gathering only for guests I {#Emph}know {#Prev}are going to be cool. Which can't explain how {#Emph}you {#Prev}keep stumbling upon it, but hey! Details, right?

1.Text: {#Emph}Whoa{#Prev}, watch with those knives, Mel baby, wouldn't want you accidentally sticking it to someone here! Though, {#Emph}wait wait wait{#Prev}, I've seen those two before...

2.Text: Perhaps you know these blades from when they belonged to the nature god called Pan. Though I didn't steal them or anything! And I'll be careful.

3.Text: Oh, yeah, {#Emph}Paaan! {#Prev}I love Pan, he is {#Emph}wild{#Prev}, and he really gets {#Emph}around! {#Prev}Even once helped Dad out with his Typhon problem way back when. You tell him I said hey! Pan, not Dad.

1.Text: Hey, it's that polecat, she's with you? Seen her pawing on the mountain here and there, just lying low, the same as me and everybody here! She got a name?

2.Text: Oh yes, I'd like to introduce you to Gale, who is a rather independent sort and has been helping scout ahead a bit. I'm impressed you knew her for a polecat right away!

3.Text: Oh I know animals, Mel baby! Why, I'm an animal myself, all of us are! Though we'll try not to act like it with Gale. And don't worry about Maena here either, she doesn't bite! Hard.

1.Text: Have you had any run-ins with Prometheus? Since Chronos wouldn't dare show his face on this mountain, he must have sent this lackey of his to keep all of Olympus occupied.

2.Text: {#Emph}Prometheus{#Prev}, he's {#Emph}back?! {#Prev}I must be out of the loop. Thought he was still strapped to some mountainside, getting his innards gnawed at by an Eagle, something nasty of the sort!

3.Text: That did supposedly occur. But he is definitely back, personally leading the vanguard trying to tear Olympus apart. If he prevails... no more feasting.

4.Text: {#Emph}Hahahaha{#Prev}, come on, baby, it can't be {#Emph}all {#Prev}that bad! What's he going to do, cook our food with the flame he took from Dad? Tell you what, next time you see him, tell him to stop by!

1.Text: Have you had any run-ins with the Titan Prometheus? Chronos was in league with him. He's been causing quite a commotion, all told.

2.Text: {#Emph}Prometheus{#Prev}, he's {#Emph}back?! {#Prev}I must be out of the loop. Thought he was still strapped to some mountainside, getting his innards gnawed at by an Eagle, something nasty of the sort!

3.Text: That did supposedly occur, but he is definitely back, personally leading the vanguard that was trying to tear Olympus apart. And he's still out there, sowing dissent.

4.Text: {#Emph}Hahahaha{#Prev}, come on, baby, it can't be {#Emph}all {#Prev}that bad! What's he going to do, cook our food with the flame he took from Dad? Tell you what, next time you see him, tell him to stop by!

1.Text: So did you have a chat with old Prometheus on my behalf or what? I'd go on over and invite him here myself, but I'm the host, {#Emph}heh! {#Prev}It wouldn't do for me to slip away, would it?

2.Text: Of all the things for you to vividly recall. You truly wanted me to direct one of our most bitter foes {#Emph}here{#Prev}, to a feast not even your closest family members know about?

3.Text: I mean... {#Emph}yeah, heh! {#Prev}We gods can be so stubborn and stuck up, waving our weapons at each other when we ought to wave an olive branch instead! Now you go tell that hothead that we're saving him a spot!

1.Text: I felt quite foolish, but did ask Prometheus on your behalf if he'd attend this feast. He already knew what I was going to say, being the Titan of Foresight and all. He sensed no ill motive... and took it for a fiendish trap for that very reason.

2.Text: And he's supposed to be one of the wiser ones? What made you all so {#Emph}cynical{#Prev}, baby? You don't trust anyone or any{#Emph}thing! {#Prev}No wonder everything is all screwed up out there!

3.Text: So you {#Emph}do {#Prev}know things are dire! I thought you weren't paying any attention, burying your head in the sand and tuning out whatever you've no wish to hear.

4.Text: You got it half right. See, I don't like to worry about the things I can't control! {#Emph}Wine{#Prev}, I can control. The quality of this feast, I {#Emph}can {#Prev}control! But all the in-fighting? {#Emph}Heh. {#Prev}Plenty of other gods who specialize in {#Emph}that.

1.Text: {#Emph}Whoa {#Prev}who's the {#Emph}bird{#Prev}, and I don't mean {#Emph}you{#Prev}, Mel baby! That raven flew in here, all skittish-looking, like it's seen a ghost! Do ravens drink? Might take the edge off just a bit.

2.Text: My raven Raki can become a little nervous around strangers... or just about anything, really. I don't think he cares for wine, although this atmosphere may do him good.

3.Text: Might do {#Emph}you {#Prev}some good too, you know. Your pets are welcome here, since we're all animals deep down, know what I mean?

1.Text: Got anybody special in your life or what Mel baby, 'cause if you just let me know, I'll get 'em in! Can easily spare one or two more invitations here!

2.Text: I appreciate the offer, thanks. I'm not bound in the way Lord Uncle Zeus and Queen Hera are if that's what you mean, but have most of my needs fulfilled.

3.Text: Well that's a way to put it. I like having all {#Emph}my {#Prev}needs met too! Long as you're also getting your {#Emph}desires {#Prev}met, but anyway, your mate or mates are welcome to stop by!

1.Text: I must admit I'm unaccustomed to seeing Satyrs that make no attempt to skewer me on sight. Old friends of yours?

2.Text: Oh yeah, all these old goats and I, we go {#Emph}way {#Prev}back! Proper Satyrs that love a proper good time. As for everything else, they just don't pay it any mind. And neither do I!

1.Text: Mel baby, we're past the small-talk stage of our relationship, so we should take the next big step: {#Emph}smaller talk!

2.Text: And what exactly is the difference between small and smaller talk? Do we lower our voices?

3.Text: Even better, we will hardly talk at all! The bond we share speaks volumes anyway! It's {#Emph}great{#Prev}, just try it, ready? {#Emph}Go!

1.Text: Sure you don't want to join us for a soak in the spring? It's cold out, yeah, but not in there! Forge of Hephaestus pumping in {#Emph}just {#Prev}the right amount of heat!

2.Text: We have a spring like this where I reside! It's very comfortable... except, I really shouldn't bathe right now. For a variety of reasons.

3.Text: And yet you keep on showing up! Come {#Emph}on {#Prev}Mel baby, you want in, no need to be shy, we're friends here, {#Emph}all {#Prev}of us! Some {#Emph}more {#Prev}than friends even! {#Emph}Heh! {#Prev}All in due time I guess?

1.Text: Now then what sort of nymph are {#Emph}you? {#Prev}Oh wait wait wait, Mel baby, I know {#Emph}you{#Prev}, just how long has it been?!

2.Text: Certainly it's been some nights, to have induced a lapse of memory. How have you fared, along with all your guests?

3.Text: Oh we've been good as grapes here, yeah? Each night's a journey through the {#Emph}mind! {#Prev}Here, think on one of {#Emph}these!

1.Text: My headmistress was a wanderer like you. She taught me something of your journeys and travails. You've crossed the world... met many different beings! Yet you'd rather be here, like this?

2.Text: {#Emph}Haha, oh {#Prev}absolutely, {#Emph}yes! {#Prev}I mean just look around you, {#Emph}everybody's {#Prev}beautiful, the weather's perfect, and we're fully stocked! What, you think I'd rather be out for a stroll?

3.Text: No, I... merely thought a life of travel might have made your disposition somewhat different! I don't know... more introspective? More solitary, perhaps.

4.Text: You're still young, baby! If you'd seen all I'd seen then you'd appreciate the finer things the same as me. No forcing it! You'll get there, maybe once all of this is over with!

1.Text: Have you any idea why this mountain has been shaking ceaselessly, doubtless to the occasional dismay of your honored guests?

2.Text: Yes I do! Sometimes the feasting gets a little rowdy, if you know what I mean, with all the dancing and whatnot! Uncle Poseidon's not the {#Emph}only {#Prev}Earth-Shaker on Olympus!

3.Text: No. {#Emph}Typhon {#Prev}has awakened! The Father of All Monsters now threatens your own father's palace. You can ignore Chronos somehow, fine. Prometheus, perhaps. But not this.

4.Text: {#Emph}Oh no! Typhon's out there, come to ruin everything! Whatever will we do?! Hahaha{#Prev}, see that, baby? Nobody {#Emph}cares! {#Prev}Whatever happens, happens! And we're gonna feast until it does, no matter what! Nice try with that one, though.

1.Text: What did you say happened to Zag, everything good with him still, yeah? You ought to bring him next you come this way, oh he'd be {#Emph}into {#Prev}it!

2.Text: I previously mentioned Chronos, our Titan grandfather who's relentlessly attacking this mountain, holds the members of my immediate family captive; Zagreus included. So he can't make it to the feast right now.

3.Text: {#Emph}Ah {#Prev}that's too bad, though maybe later, yeah? I've always felt a bond with him, a real connection, so if you see the Zag man, let him know he's welcome to my feast here {#Emph}anytime!

1.Text: Sounds as though you and my brother Zagreus were fairly close. What was he like? Seeing as I have no real memory of him, since Chronos took him back when I was very small.

2.Text: You know I haven't heard from him in quite a while, yeah? {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, come to think of it, we never really talked too much, although I sent him lots of Boons! How is he anyway?

1.Text: How is the Zag man lately anyway, is everything all right with him? Stopped sending him my Boons a while back...

2.Text: Well now that Zagreus is freed from temporal imprisonment, along with my mother, father, and the House of Hades staff, I think he's doing very well! I'm certain he'd be pleased to hear from you.

3.Text: Well that is a relief as I thought maybe I offended in some way! He could have gone and cut me off, but he did not.

1.Text: Things are happening all over but this is the only happening place on {#Emph}this {#Prev}mountain, baby.
Just one drink isn't going to hurt! It's going to do the {#Emph}opposite{#Prev}, you'll see!
Can't stay and hang out, you got places to go, people to see, I get it, baby!
You look like you're having a night! And wouldn't you know it, so am {#Emph}I!
Been going for a while here, baby, and we plan to {#Emph}keep {#Prev}going till all this is over!
Come on now, relax and have a drink, {#Emph}mingle {#Prev}a bit, this is a {#Emph}feast{#Prev}, you know!
Remember, don't go telling Dad about this little gathering of ours, all right?
You're always welcome here but not your worries, baby, you leave those behind!
Hey, pull yourself together, baby, we're just getting started!
Sure you don't want to take a quick dip in the spring? It'll warm you right up!
This mountain isn't going anywhere, and neither are we!
Come all this way and can't even hang out, that's just not right, baby!
If you're sick of all the fighting, I've got {#Emph}just {#Prev}the thing for you!
The water's nice and warm, but if you don't want to take a dip, it's cool!
I'd ask you tell the fam I told them cheers but that might get a little awkward, yeah?
Leave your worries at the gate and have yourself a cup of something, {#Emph}here!
Know that all of us are with you {#Emph}all {#Prev}the way, so cheers to your success!
Take it from me, there is {#Emph}never {#Prev}a bad time for a good feast!
Wait wait wait weren't you just here? It's all a blur for me!
No use fighting the inevitable when you're thirsty, yeah?
Take a load off, relax, have a drink and all that! The night's still young!
Well don't just stand there, eat! Drink! Whatever you fancy!
The moon is shining, the water's warm, the Nectar's flowing, what is not to like?
You keep on showing up but never stick around, quit {#Emph}teasing {#Prev}us, baby!
Hey Mel baby, you're bringing down the mood a bit looking like that, you get me, yeah?
Oh you missed a {#Emph}real {#Prev}good time last night... or might have been the night before...
Everybody! It's the Zag man's sister, let's all give her a warm welcome, yeah?
Oh you missed such a good time, baby, but more good times are always to be had!
Just be cool, Mel baby, everybody's doing their thing so let's do ours here, yeah?
Think I've got one of your favorites somewhere, is it maybe one of these?
You want to be your best out there, so take a breather and recharge a bit, you know?
Sure I can get you Boons and all but let me know if I can get you a massage!
Weren't you just here, baby, or have we been feasting all night long?
Remember, don't let on to anybody that we're here, they'll never understand!
Do let me know if I can get you anything besides the usual stuff, yeah?
Whatever you're craving, we probably have it somewhere around here!
Don't look now but one of the Satyrs there, I think he fancies you!
So cool of you stop by our exclusive get-together here, always a treat, baby!
See all the Nymphs and Satyrs there? Hey I could make an introduction if you like!
{#Emph}Whoa-hoho{#Prev}, either I had a few too many there... or I just haven't had enough!

Now who is {#Emph}this{#Prev}, what sort of Nymph do we have here? Not from the waters nor the woods, but wait wait {#Emph}wait! {#Prev}Those {#Emph}eyes! {#Prev}Zag, man, is that {#Emph}you?! {#Prev}You've {#Emph}changed! {#Prev}I like it!

2.Text: Lord Dionysus, I presume? I'm Melinoë, sister to Zagreus. I've come to the mountain's aid at the family's behest! But, what is the meaning of this festivity? Aren't you at war?

3.Text: {#Emph}Ohhh, Mel{#Prev}, right, the others mentioned you. {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, listen baby, I'm into {#Emph}lots {#Prev}of different things, but war just isn't one of them. What's the use, we gods can't die! But we can {#Emph}live!

4.Text: Your mountain is under siege. Chronos took my side of the family, and soon he may take yours!

1.Text: Now who is {#Emph}this{#Prev}, what sort of Nymph do we have here? Not from the waters nor the woods, but wait wait {#Emph}wait! {#Prev}Those {#Emph}eyes! {#Prev}Zag, man, is that {#Emph}you?! {#Prev}You've {#Emph}changed! {#Prev}I like it!

2.Text: Lord Dionysus, I presume? I'm Melinoë, sister to Zagreus. I've been coming to the mountain's aid at the family's behest. Why all the festivity? The end of the war?

3.Text: {#Emph}Ohhh, Mel{#Prev}, right, the others mentioned you. {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, listen baby, I'm into {#Emph}lots {#Prev}of different things, but war just isn't one of them. What's the use, we gods can't die! But we can {#Emph}live!

4.Text: I said the {#Emph}end {#Prev}of the war. Though I suppose your mountain technically still is under siege.

5.Text: All the more reason to raise a cup while we still can, yeah? {#Emph}Heh. {#Prev}Though I get it! Not your thing. But why not have a little pick-me-up for the road ahead?

1.Text: Mel baby, you look like hell if you don't mind me saying, I mean what did you fall down the mountainside on your way here? Care to wash up?

2.Text: Please pardon my disheveled state. I had to cross a doomed city of the risen dead, infiltrate an enemy armada, and climb halfway to the Palace of Zeus to get here.

3.Text: No excuses! Now either get out of that positively ripe dress you've got on and make like all my other guests, or move along! We enforce a strict code of attire.

1.Text: Been hearing wild tales from outside, can you back any of it up, baby? Something about the {#Emph}dawning of another age?

2.Text: A recent prophecy from the Three Fates. They have foreseen a distant time when mortals won't be as beholden to the gods... perhaps that shall be cause for a real feast.

3.Text: {#Emph}You're {#Prev}thinking maybe all the other gods will end up feasting {#Emph}here! {#Prev}Then we'll have better things to do than pushing mortalkind around. And it'll be a {#Emph}prophecy fulfilled!

1.Text: I think you should be able to come out now, as the greatest threats facing your mountain are gone for the most part. Well, granted there are vicious Satyrs out there still.

2.Text: Hey, easy with the Satyr talk, it really isn't cool! You think my Satyr friends here ever talk that way about us gods? And what do you mean, {#Emph}greatest threats?

3.Text: Typhon, the Father of All Monsters; Chronos, the Titan of Time; the former utterly destroyed, the latter pacified. The war is {#Emph}over! {#Prev}Olympus is secure!

4.Text: The war is {#Emph}over?! {#Prev}Hear that everybody, the war is {#Emph}over! {#Prev}If that's not cause for celebration, I don't know what is, so grab a {#Emph}drink{#Prev}, take a {#Emph}dip{#Prev}, shake your {#Emph}hips{#Prev}, you know it, {#Emph}yeah!

1.Text: You won't be leaving here will you.
No way, baby!
Dionysus, won't you at least notify your family members that you're well? Some of them must be concerned for you.

2.Text: I'm sure I'll get around to it one of these nights, baby, but we're still celebrating your success, {#Emph}you won the war!

3.Text: I did not personally win the war. We stood together as a family and prevailed. I merely did my part.

4.Text: And I am doing {#Emph}my {#Prev}part right now! The others know I'm going to be fine, I just need a little space what with all the excitement... a little space with all these {#Emph}fabulous guests!

1.Text: Hey, wait wait wait, hold on, if you're not jesting that whatever war was on is over, then how come you keep showing up to get these battle-ready Boons from me?

2.Text: ...Suffice it to say there are still battles to be won. But I'll spare you the details, for the sake of your sanity and mine.

3.Text: Well cheers I've not much sanity to spare! Sounds like you'll be around, you've got the special pass, so stop by anytime!

1.Text: You're a most-gracious host.

2.Text: Happy feasting, my lord.

1.Text: {#Emph}Heeey.

2.Text: {#Emph}Heeey!

3.Text: What is up?

4.Text: Cheers!

5.Text: Oh I'm not going anywhere.

1.Text: Come on!

2.Text: Oh come off it.

3.Text: I almost spilled this!

4.Text: Hey now.

5.Text: Take it {#Emph}easy!

12.Text: Do we have to escort you out?

1.Text: If only I could learn to let go as you have, Dionysus...
I already have plans this evening, sorry...

2.Text: He's great, I'm sure...

3.Text: ...I'm going to have to pass.

4.Text: ...Yeah.

5.Text: No, I... {#Emph}ugh.

8.Text: If I ever encounter him, sure.

1.Text: Get a load of these.

2.Text: Let's see here...

3.Text: What have we got...

4.Text: Got just the thing...

5.Text: Got what you need...

1.Text: I know you cannot hear me, but... if you have comforted my father in his plight, thank you.
Leave it be.

2.Text: The boulder has seen punishment enough.

3.Text: Cease this, Daughter.

4.Text: Vent your frustrations elsewhere.

1.Text: {#Emph}Three-headed Cerberus permits none approach, neither him nor his master.
{#Emph}The monstrous Hound of Hell bares countless fangs as if to say, back off.
{#Emph}Feared watch-dog Cerberus regards the Princess with his six expectant eyes.
{#Emph}The multiheaded monster keeps his fury well in check beside the rightful Underworld King.
{#Emph}Fierce hell-hound Cerberus has many fangs but little trust to spare.
{#Emph}The resting hound of hell makes plain he wishes not to be disturbed.
{#Emph}Three-headed Cerberus eyes every surface of the chamber, all at once.
{#Emph}The savage watch dog looks tentatively at the Princess of the Underworld.
{#Emph}Notoriously vicious Cerberus sits vigilantly by his master's side.
{#Emph}The triple-headed guardian of hell does not wish to be troubled at this time.
{#Emph}The brutal hound of hell by now permits the Princess of the Dead to approach.
{#Emph}Where goes the lord and master of the dead, the infernal watchdog of the Underworld follows.
{#Emph}The one-time guardian of the gates of hell restrains his viciousness for the Princess.
{#Emph}For unknown reasons does this savage beast decide not to devour the Princess.
{#Emph}Somehow the Princess of the Underworld has worked her magick on the hound of hell.
{#Emph}The Infernal Beast that wrought such terror in the Mourning Fields now sits there calmly and expectantly, not for the Princess of the Underworld, but someone else.
{#Emph}Ferocious Cerberus yet guards his master dutifully, having discovered him within these depths.
That won't earn his affection.

2.Text: Leave him be.

3.Text: {#Emph}Stay{#Prev}, Cerberus...

4.Text: He wishes to be left alone.

5.Text: A temperamental beast.

6.Text: He does not wish to play.

1.Text: {#Emph}The notoriously fearsome triple-headed monster Cerberus rests in his favored spot, and now regards the Princess of the Dead with three expressions different than before.

2.Text: Well boy, this must be the next best thing to guarding the Underworld's gates. Say, do I have your permission to give you a scratch? The way my brother demonstrated before.

1.Speaker: NPC_Zagreus_Past_01
1.Text: Well this is a rare treat. The both of you together in this lounge! What brings you here, Grandfather?

2.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
2.Text: I yet seek the girl's whereabouts, is what! I have turned over this residence in its entirety, and found nary a sign! She is already as elusive as you always were, Hades.

3.Speaker: NPC_LordHades_01
3.Text: That or your old senses have dulled. She went running over there by the Head Chef, where she yet lingers in silence. Go, before her patience wears thin.

4.Speaker: NPC_Zagreus_Past_01
4.Text: {#Emph}Erm... {#Prev}what Father meant to say was, {#Emph}no, we've no idea where my good son's little sister is! {#Prev}She could be anywhere! Have you tried checking the administrative chamber? Gods, I sound like Hypnos.

1.Text: I do appreciate the hint.
Keep up the good work!
Where are you, my girl...?
{#Emph}<Laugh>
...When I was having difficulties with my son... sometimes I thought of you, Father. I could not fathom having had more children to contend with all at once.

2.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
2.Text: Yes, well... I was not terribly successful at contending with you lot, now, was I? Particularly Zeus... to think that I shall see him and the others again soon.

3.Text: I can make no assurances about how you shall be received. These dreamlike memories we share did not reach Mount Olympus, it seems. But Zeus does have my full report.

4.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
4.Text: Surely a ringing endorsement! But I merely jest. If Time can be so cruel, then it is only fitting for his children to be much the same. Would you not agree, Granddaughter?

5.Text: We may have more in common than we'd like to admit. But in any event, Lord Uncle Zeus asked you to come alone. Only the Fates now know what lies in store... although there's still no sign of them, even with Nyx's aid?

6.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
6.Text: None. I cast them into the abyss. Had I known precisely where, they would have known how to get back. Yet if my hypothesis about such possibilities as we experienced is correct... we may find them.

7.Text: We shall. And I look forward to testing this hypothesis. Perhaps we'll all learn something about ourselves.

8.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
8.Text: Would that we could! Gods and Titans may be doomed to live forever... but we need not be bound to our old ways.

9.Text: Indeed. {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, Father...? Thank you for all your hospitality. It gladdens me to see you doing well.

10.Text: I would not be if not for you, Daughter. I trust that we shall see each other again soon. And perhaps even you, Father.

11.Speaker: NPC_Chronos_01
11.Text: Likewise, Hades. At least this House is mostly to your preference again. Beyond these halls, of course, much more is to be done.

12.Text: Yes, well... Father, I wish you the best with the ongoing Underworld renovations. As for us, our chariot is here.

1.Text: That it is. I am prepared.
Shadows conceal you.
Be well, Lord Father.
Greetings.

2.Text: Hail, Daughter.

3.Text: Darkness suits me best.

4.Text: Go unseen.

5.Text: Shadows conceal you.

1.Text: Please, take it.
Thank you both for this.
Father, while I know this wasn't necessarily permitted, I thought if maybe it would be of any comfort at all, that I might offer you this Nectar?

2.Text: Exactly like your brother, blast... I fear I'm not in any mood or state for such a thing. Concern yourself not with my comfort, but with the target of your wrath.

1.Text: Mother, Father, I'm so grateful to have you back in my life. We've so much to catch up on, but all the time in the world. For now, this is just a small House-warming gift.

2.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
2.Text: Oh {#Emph}thank {#Prev}you, this is {#Emph}perfect! {#Prev}Our supply back at the House has disappeared... perhaps Chronos had a taste for it.

3.Text: Nectar from the highest peaks... to think we once forbade this substance here, though that was well before your time. Thank you, Daughter. And we have something here for you, in turn. A small token, but a symbol of our family as well.

1.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
1.Text: Thank you, Daughter. We could certainly make use of this. Hades had a particular idea for it, in fact.

2.Text: If you would permit it, Daughter... I would offer up such Nectar to the Shades assisting in the Underworld renovations underway. As an added token of appreciation for their toil. Is that acceptable to you?

3.Text: Of course, Father, it's yours to do with as you please. And I can think of no finer purpose for it than to reward those Shades who have remained loyal to us through all this.

1.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
1.Text: Such a fine bottle. We graciously accept! You know, you remind me of your brother sometimes...

2.Text: These customs that we share from those above... I ask that you not follow our traditions blindly. Such traditions may be partially responsible for the many mistakes that led us to this point.

3.Text: I share your cautious feeling about this, Father, but... of the many traditions of the gods, the act of giving Nectar to those we care for seems one of the better ones, in my estimation.

1.Text: ...Perhaps so.
You ought have many others who would welcome such a gift. To have been raised in the seclusion of those Crossroads... I fear it must have been a very solitary life. More so than one would like.

2.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
2.Text: Solitude is not always such a bad thing, but... certainly it couldn't have been easy on you.

3.Text: You need have no such fear. Growing up in the Crossroads was never easy, but... I never felt alone. I always had somebody or something to confide in... I would speak sometimes even to a fountain that we have in your honor.

4.Text: Your words are not as persuasive to me as either one of us would like. If you had grown up in my House, you would have been showered with attention, not forced to harden your hands with toil... especially for one so young.

5.Text: I have never regretted what I had to do, Father. And what friendships I have, I cherish. Perhaps I could have grown up with more, but I had everything I needed. Besides my parents. And brother and dog.

1.Text: And now you have us, too.
Thank the Fates.
I know some of the Nectar's going to our loyal Shades, but I would like for you and Mother to enjoy this one yourselves. Whenever the occasion fits, just... sometime.

2.Text: The occasion for such pleasantries... perhaps after our Underworld renovations are complete, and we have taken proper stock of our resources and the Shades, then finally we may accept a moment of reprieve.

3.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
3.Text: Oh, stop it, Hades. Surely we can make good on Melinoë's request sooner than that. You know better than anyone that the toil never ends, so the moments of reprieve have to be seized when they present themselves.

4.Text: Thus speaks the Queen. Thank you for this, Daughter. But you truly need not spare such thoughts on us. We have each other once again. I myself have want for nothing more.

1.Text: Now that you've had a Nectar for a small occasion of some sort, I did also want to give you this. For a more-special time, perhaps long from now, after we've practically forgotten how it was living apart, and the circumstances call for merriment.

2.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
2.Text: This is... Ambrosia, and with such a hue as could have only come from the source... Daughter, {#Emph}thank you...!

3.Text: Ambrosia from the heavens themselves... I scarce remember its savor. But I never shall forget what it was like living apart. Nor should any of us long for Time to take the pain of it away. Let us remember always how we reached this point together.

4.Text: When I was little, Lady Hecate said something similar... that the pain of the past shall always linger, though assert itself less frequently with age. Well then, perhaps we ought to celebrate the memory itself. An aeon from now, for all I care.

5.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
5.Text: A celebration an aeon from now would leave us with plenty of time for preparation, so... why not, Hades? Ambrosia such as this ought to age nicely till then.

6.Text: Please let me know if I can help with any of the planning when the time comes. Or if there's anything else I can do while you're getting the House back in order.

7.Speaker: NPC_Persephone_01
7.Text: It's we who should be asking this of you. When you were born, Hades and I thanked the Fates that we were blessed with such a child. But we had positively no idea...

1.Text: Thank you both...!
I used to have a sense for all the blessings of our kin; their Boons were not permitted in this realm. That sense has dulled, for only now do I detect the influence of Ares here...

2.Text: Your sense for surface blessings is intact, Father. I met Ares only after all the rest. It seems this war has taken such a turn that he's now helping put a stop to it.

3.Text: Is that what he told you...? The only reason I can think of that my nephew would endeavor to conclude a war is if it meant still-greater wars could then be waged instead. Nevertheless, if he is claiming to be on your side, he would not lie outright.

1.Text: I used to have a sense for all the blessings of our kin; their Boons were not permitted in this realm. That sense has dulled, for only now do I detect the influence of Ares here...

2.Text: Your sense for surface blessings is intact, Father. I met Ares only after all the rest.

3.Text: The only reason I can think of that my nephew would endeavor to conclude a war is if it meant still-greater wars could then be waged instead. Nevertheless, if he is claiming to be on your side, he would not lie outright.

1.Text: To think that you have seen Olympus with your own eyes... your brother never had that opportunity. And I myself... my life is here, and I've no memories of mountaintops.

2.Text: It must have been a sight to behold, once. Now it's beset with the Titan's legions, and mindless Automaton defenders that want {#Emph}me {#Prev}destroyed just as much as our foes.

3.Text: I told them never to depend on such contraptions! A proper army needs to be driven by glory, if not fear. Their Automatons feel {#Emph}nothing! {#Prev}How well can they possibly fight?

1.Text: Where's Cerberus, Father? He's usually right here. I saw him in the Fields as before!

2.Text: He runs amok at my behest. Spreads the attention of the Titan's legions thin. Eventually they drive him back, but can do him no harm.

3.Text: So just you and the boulder, then. Looking as though it's not been heaved up any hills in quite a while. Chronos doesn't make you do it?

4.Text: I'd have less difficult a time than a mere Shade. Besides, these shackles cannot be unlocked, save by the Titan's command. But I'd remain here for eternity before I'd grovel at his feet.

5.Text: You say this boulder was companion to a mortal king? I... sense something from it. There can be so much energy within a common stone.

6.Text: I'll take you at your word. The boulder and I... we're not as close as was its last relationship. Though perhaps you shall coax something from it; the Witch apparently has taught you everything.

1.Text: Where's Cerberus, Father? He's usually right here. I saw him in the Fields as before!

2.Text: He runs amok at my behest. Spreads the attention of the Titan's legions thin. Eventually they drive him back, but can do him no harm.

3.Text: So just you and the boulder, then. Looking as though it's not been heaved up any hills in quite a while. You say this boulder was companion to a mortal king? I... sense something from it. There can be so much energy within a common stone.

4.Text: I'll take you at your word. The boulder and I... we're not as close as was its last relationship. Though perhaps you shall coax something from it; the Witch apparently has taught you everything.

1.Text: Has that boulder yet revealed anything to you? I know not why I ask, mere baseless superstition on my part... but I have seen you go to it from time to time.

2.Text: You spoke gently of the prisoner once held here, as though you had forgiven him. I used to think that was impossible in Tartarus. The boulder now reminds me otherwise.

3.Text: Most of the wretches who we once held captive here had no hope of forgiveness or freedom at all, yet even they broke loose, if undeservedly. Then let the boulder stand as testament to all that has transpired, and shall come to pass.

1.Text: My brothers each are aiding you, are they? Zeus, doubtless leading from behind the safety of his palace walls... Poseidon, blustering as though his victory is already at hand...

2.Text: Father, they're fighting to defend their home... and they're fighting for {#Emph}you! {#Prev}You're right that neither one is much inclined to show concern, but why should they? Fear spreads.

3.Text: They sat oblivious upon their surface realm for far too long...! But do not listen to my rantings about them. Had you known your own brother, perhaps you'd better understand the impulse for such ill-conceived remarks...

1.Text: What has that blasted Titan done to Cerberus, that he should storm into this place with such abandon, only to be ushered out again? Takes a small army of Satyrs to drive him back...

2.Text: Chronos casts him out into the Mourning Fields above. Then rage and despair congeal about him, and his better senses take leave. My own path leads me through where he resides.

3.Text: So you must face him in that sorry state. Thank you, Daughter, for taking pity on the moody beast. He has seen better, but been through worse. You were too young to form a bond before, but perhaps... it is not too late.

1.Text: Cerberus has been quite agitated, and I'm realizing why. It's not just having to roam through the Mourning Fields; he probably can sense Typhon's return.

2.Text: Just about every monster I've confronted probably is traceable to Typhon in some way. I doubt he had a close relationship with any of his kin; not even Cerberus.

3.Text: I doubt that too. It seems not one of us is able to escape our fathers' influence. Yet here we all are, still.

1.Text: ...The scent of blood. You're injured. And you expect to face the Titan still? At least you're in the right place should you die.

2.Text: I won't be dying here no matter what. As for my injuries, perhaps Lord Charon has some Life Essence in stock.

3.Text: Even now, the Boatman plies his trade? Absurd. Our entire operation was shut down! Although... I ought remember that he serves this realm, not me.

1.Text: Who else besides Prometheus does Chronos have under his thumb? I would know every last Titan or such ilk who deigned to turn on us.

2.Text: Besides marauding hordes of Satyrs and such, the ones that come to mind include the Cyclops Polyphemus... and Nyx's daughter Eris... though she may be acting on her own.

3.Text: Strife could never be controlled, Nyx knew only too well. As for that Cyclops... he and your Uncle Poseidon have some history that may have spurred his impulses. Well... it is not yet the longest list of enemies, at least.

1.Text: Such a cacophony occurred, after you last visited. Exactly when I cannot say. All of the Titan's wretched servants flew into a panic. Their cries would not cease. What transpired?

2.Text: Perhaps they were concerned for their master. Or busy trying to bring him back to life. Because I slew him, finally. And it won't be the last time.

3.Text: Blood and darkness, {#Emph}hah... urgh! {#Prev}Then you accomplished... that which once took half the blasted strength of Olympus... all on your own.

4.Text: Not on my own at all. I had their strength, if not their support; as you've given me yours. Father, we can stop him. And for now... we can kill him.

5.Text: He shall seek vengeance with a renewed zeal. This entire plot of his is driven by the same impulse. Then, kill him if you must. At least... his many deaths ought keep him occupied.

1.Text: Such a cacophony occurred, after you last visited. Exactly when I cannot say. All of the Titan's wretched servants flew into a panic. Their cries would not cease. What transpired?

2.Text: Perhaps they were concerned for their master. Or busy trying to bring him back to life. Because I slew him once again. And it won't be the last time.

3.Text: Blood and darkness, {#Emph}hah! Urgh... {#Prev}To have achieved such an outcome... which once required half the blasted strength of all Olympus, on your own...

4.Text: Not on my own at all. I had their strength, if not their support; as you've given me yours. Father, we can stop him. And for now... we can kill him.

5.Text: He shall seek vengeance with a renewed zeal. This entire plot of his is driven by the same impulse. Then, kill him if you must. At least... his many deaths ought keep him occupied.

1.Text: When Chronos took our family and the House, and you bade the Witch of the Crossroads take me... I remember it somehow, or dreamt of it. Did he... demand you tell him of the Fates?

2.Text: How could you possibly...? Perhaps the Fates themselves permitted you that bit of insight. My father sought them, but I revealed nothing. Couldn't have even if I so desired, for no one knows where those three are, save {#Emph}them.

3.Text: Wait, you never told Chronos how to find the Fates? Then how {#Emph}did {#Prev}he? Because he's captured them. Not long ago, perhaps, but nonetheless. I'm certain of it.

4.Text: What?! No... but if this is true, well then my father's plan for conquest is much closer to fruition than I thought. If not even they could stop him... Daughter, what chance do {#Emph}you {#Prev}have...?

1.Text: You saw what happened... what Chronos did to Mother, and my brother, and the rest. Where are they? Where is he holding them?

2.Text: My knowledge of this is not up-to-date. He... made everybody stop, somehow. I saw them, still as stone; not petrified exactly but ensnared, in the Great Hall of the House. He must have stored them someplace else inside...

3.Text: Even when I'm able to vanquish Chronos on a given night, most of the House is sealed off, and I'm unable to remain for long. How can we break them out...?

4.Text: Perhaps if you ask the Titan very nicely, he shall comply? Daughter, I know of no way to undo his work, and have no wisdom to impart. But {#Emph}this{#Prev}, I can provide.

1.Text: Daughter, tell me what... became of the Witch of the Crossroads, should you know. When all seemed lost... your mother and I, we left you in her care.

2.Text: And she has cared for me ever since. Prepared me. Though, we had best not speak of her in these chambers. Suffice it to say, the Unseen remain in shadow.

3.Text: Good. She was... well as you say, we'd best say nothing more. Though if you have the opportunity, extend to her my deepest gratitude.

1.Text: Father, wanted to ask about your nephew Heracles. In my run-ins with him, he had mentioned something about visiting you and Cerberus here in the Underworld...

2.Text: {#Emph}Bah{#Prev}, Heracles! He hauled Cerberus bodily up to the surface, did he tell you that? Not by his choice, he claimed, but still! I could not believe my eyes when he hoisted that dog.

3.Text: You permitted it to happen? Was Cerberus all right?

4.Text: Look at him, of course he was all right. And I permitted that brute only because what he did ought have been impossible! Apparently the incident remains a source of pride.

1.Text: It may be best to keep your distance there, or rather for that dog. Although... the Witch of the Crossroads, she once had a hound much like that one...

2.Text: Then this must be the very same. She's called Hecuba, and I'm certain she'll be respectful both to you and Cerberus. Besides, they already met in the Fields...

3.Text: A creature possessed of loyalty and courage, then. A quite-uncommon combination, whether in beasts or otherwise. Be on your best behavior with her, Cerberus.

1.Text: If you'd indulge a senseless curiosity... how fares my House? Your brother, he was more or less in charge of the decor. I highly doubt the Titan shares his taste.

2.Text: Well, unless Zagreus was enamored of gold trim and the Titan's sneering likeness everywhere, then it's probably quite different from what you recall...

3.Text: {#Emph}Urgh... {#Prev}you have your mother's candor to a fault. You ought have told me everything was {#Emph}fine! {#Prev}The comfort of lies at times is all we have.

1.Text: Daughter. Tell me something of yourself, for I know not a thing. For instance... what is it that you like to do? When you are not... attempting this.

2.Text: What do I like to do? Well... I ensure all of my reagents are in order, so when practicing my craft, what I need is always close at hand. And I like to... {#Emph}ungh{#Prev}, Father, this rings false...

3.Text: {#Emph}Mm. {#Prev}Neither the time nor place for trivialities... perhaps, however, at some point... we may discuss such matters more. But there are scores to settle first.

1.Text: Most fear to tread within this chamber, but quite recently the visage of Nyx herself charged in. Saluted in a huff and strode on past! One of Nyx's daughters?

2.Text: That sounds like Nemesis. She's wanted to get her hands on Chronos practically more than I ever did. Going after the traces of him now, the same as me. We have a thing going.

3.Text: That almost makes me feel some pity for those traces, then. To have to face Retribution or Vengeance, if not both.

1.Text: Has Chronos... my father... has he been amenable to your requirements in all of this? No sudden or discernible changes of behavior or demeanor?

2.Text: He's been himself... his newer self, that is. Rather contrite, and I daresay enthusiastic about alleviating the negative effects that still linger here and above.

3.Text: We ought remain on guard nevertheless. Although, my father never could hide his contempt. If you have rid him of that... then he truly is no longer the Titan I once knew.

1.Text: How is Grandfather faring in the Isles of the Blessed? I was pleased to learn Lord Uncle Zeus and you were even able to find him an available post there.

2.Text: ...My father is, surprisingly, quite competent in this newfound regard, at least thus far. The work itself is not too burdensome, although the residents of the Isles of the Blessed can be very demanding.

3.Text: So Grandfather is looking after the most vaunted of Elysium, making certain that their needs are met, that sort of thing?

4.Text: Essentially, that is correct. He is attentive to detail, and not prone to forgetfulness. We shall be monitoring him to ensure he remains that way.

1.Text: Nyx, herself... even she was powerless against the Titan. Two of Night Incarnate's own sons served in my House along with her... I suppose he has them, too.

2.Text: No, Hypnos is with {#Emph}us! {#Prev}Fast asleep for all this time, perhaps some sort of... defensive response, for we have found no way to wake him. Brave Schelemeus is with us as well!

3.Text: Hypnos, asleep {#Emph}again? {#Prev}And I've no recollection of that other name... but Time has worn on me. Regardless, if the Witch yet leads the Unseen, the will of Night is not yet lost.

1.Text: It hurts my heart to see you like this, Father. But, it brings me peace. And strength. Helps that this chamber isn't crawling with Satyrs...

2.Text: Oh they have sense enough to keep their distance from me... or perhaps Cerberus. Well if seeing me in this pitiable state should spur you to your fullest wrath, then so be it.

3.Text: That's not quite it; I don't feel loathing or hatred. Elsewhere in Tartarus, perhaps, but not here. Not anymore. I just hope my presence doesn't cause you further pain.

4.Text: No. The only pain... is that your mother and I, your brother, this dog, that we were not... we could not be there to see you grow. Each time I see you now... it fills an absence that was there.

1.Text: Your mother was so proud when you were born. We... did not always think that we would have another child. But we decided to try again.

2.Text: And you did the most important thing parents can do. You {#Emph}protected {#Prev}me. As for my mother, I know her beautiful smile. The way she's looking at me in the painting that I have.

3.Text: The painting, it survived?! The Witch, she must have taken it... and such a risk, for such a thing. Know that your mother's radiance... cannot be captured. No matter the artist's skill.

1.Text: That skull you have in hand, is that... how did you come to possess it? It once had been entrusted to your mother's care... for her protection, and in a way, yours.

2.Text: Mother's Aspect of the Argent Skull Revaal deemed me a worthy-enough bearer... but it was Headmistress Hecate who first gathered the Nocturnal Arms for my task.

3.Text: Forged by the Fates! Who so like playing us for fools. That skull did not protect the Queen as much as I would have preferred; but perhaps its work merely is not yet complete.

1.Text: Your mother sends you her warmest regards, and regrets that she was unable to join me here this time. Certain matters at the House require {#Emph}her {#Prev}attention, if not mine.

2.Text: Thank you, and please give my regards to Mother, in kind. So you get to be {#Emph}here {#Prev}while she takes care of things {#Emph}there... {#Prev}do you draw lots to determine who does what?

3.Text: Drawing lots is how I wound up in this realm, and is not something I have done again. This is simpler, besides: Being here is how I can best ensure your continued success.

1.Text: Daughter, answer me something. How is it that the Titan's armies are well-organized enough to siege Olympus, when the Titan himself cowers here in Tartarus?

2.Text: We have another Titan to contend with there: Prometheus is leading the attack. I don't know how exactly he got free, or what he truly wants... other than vengeance on the gods.

3.Text: Is vengeance on the gods an insufficient desire in itself? I wanted nothing to do with his sentencing... but your Lord Uncle Zeus, he... well, he would always claim that he could fashion more-creative punishments than I...

1.Text: The darkness stirs in such a way as I've not felt since very long ago. This cannot be the Titan's work. It must be that of the Witch of the Crossroads, if not you.

2.Text: Father: {#Emph}In shadow, I serve; to shadow, I return. {#Prev}Thus have I sworn the Oath of the Unseen, who serve this realm, and execute the will of Night.

3.Text: I know less of the Unseen than you suppose. As it should be, lest the Titan could have learned much more. Then, may you serve the will of Night judiciously...

1.Text: This chamber... it once held a prisoner of mine. A mortal king who had attempted to cheat Death! I forced the wretch to heave that boulder up that path forever. He forgave me anyway.

2.Text: Forget him, Father. What purpose does it serve to dwell on some dead mortal now? Chronos wants you to wallow in your guilt. Don't.

3.Text: You misunderstand. The prisoner, he was called Sisyphus the King. His boulder there was like a friend. He... asked his friend to keep me company. Until more company arrived, he said.

4.Text: Well then I'm grateful to that boulder and the king. Chronos must not have accounted for your former prisoners being fond of you.

5.Text: Oh most of them are not. Some chose to join the Titan's legions and remain here in Tartarus. Not anywhere I cast my gaze, of course.

1.Text: How... how is it you already have my blessing, Daughter? Is that... you have our family's heirloom... the Jeweled Pom. Where did you get it?

2.Text: I... I don't remember where I got it, I... haven't I always had it? Father... I... didn't you... I don't understand.

3.Text: Most likely the Witch of the Crossroads procured it, but who can say? My father's influence is strong... Time wears on memory, perhaps. But here... I can add to its power.

1.Text: I cannot believe that I am asking but, how fares Olympus in all this? Even trapped within this chamber, it is evident to me that the Titan's legions are at war.

2.Text: The surface swarms with the dead, and the armies of Chronos are besieging the mountain. Our family is holding them back. I've been trying to break the stalemate in their favor, but all in all, it's not a pretty sight up there right now.

3.Text: {#Emph}Not a pretty sight up there... {#Prev}you mean to say you've seen all this firsthand? {#Emph}How?

4.Text: You mean our birthright. Would you believe I learned a means by which I could withstand the surface climate for a while? Long enough to make a difference up there... or to try.

5.Text: Impossible... yet seemingly, all these impossibilities continue to occur. So you must vanquish the Titan, as well as come to the rescue of Olympus. How utterly absurd that you are burdened with all that....

1.Text: Father, I'm afraid the matter on Olympus is more dire than we thought... for Chronos reawakened Typhon, who is very, {#Emph}very {#Prev}large... and dead-set on destroying the Palace of Zeus.

2.Text: {#Emph}Pah! {#Prev}Such a predictable and reckless action on the Titan's part. Although your uncle Zeus may not be quite as spry as when he and that monster previously clashed.

3.Text: You don't seem so surprised. How did you all defeat Typhon before? I've never fought something like him.

4.Text: Nor should you fight something like him, Daughter! Let Zeus clean up his mess. His thunderbolt proved quite effective in the past... although you'd think that an embodiment of storms and rage would be immune.

5.Text: I'm not about to abandon our family to face this threat on their own.

6.Text: Then you're in the wrong place. For if you think thwarting the Titan shall stop Typhon in turn, you're wrong. A monster such as that cannot be controlled. Go, see for yourself.

1.Text: What news of Typhon recently, Daughter? Zeus used to boast of how he vanquished that monstrosity alone. Now I imagine more of a concerted effort is required.

2.Text: Father, if you bear some grudge with Uncle Zeus, that's only to the benefit of all our enemies. Typhon yet threatens the mountaintop... he can be driven back, but never for long.

3.Text: We buried him under a mountain once; no ordinary show of strength, for other methods failed. Well, I trust my brother has some sort of {#Emph}plan. {#Prev}He never lacked for those.

1.Text: ...When first we had to fend off Typhon long ago, we dared not think the Titan Lord whom we had already disposed of was responsible. Surely not even {#Emph}he {#Prev}in all his arrogance believed that such a monster would bend to his will!

2.Text: All Chronos probably expected was that the monster would immediately attack Olympus. How could he have awakened such a thing without our family even noticing?

3.Text: With Nyx herself amongst the Titan Lord's captives, all that transpires deep within the Earth cannot be known by anyone. And now... even though both Typhon and the Titan fell to us before... we have never had to face them both at once.

1.Text: I have not seen you in some time... perhaps you've been preoccupied with thwarting Typhon as he makes attempts to break into my brother's nigh-impenetrable mountain palace.

2.Text: That's a rather accurate assessment of my recent outings, yes. Typhon may appear to be invincible, but there's not a creature alive that likes repeatedly being struck in the face.

3.Text: An age-old tactic that served well your predecessors in the greatest battles of their youth. I had a feeling that would be the case; in the end, little changes with time.

1.Text: ...My father... he visited me recently. Demanding that I tell him where to find you. I made clear I did not know. But you are drawing more of his attention.

2.Text: You're saying he tortured you, that blasted wretch. He won't need to find me; I'm about to find him.

3.Text: Do not misunderstand... we merely spoke. Granted, that is a rarity in itself. He never knew what to do with my brothers or me... never should have had us at all.

4.Text: Father, please don't speak that way. What even happened with you all...? I know the tales of how you vanquished him, but... know so little of how it was for you growing up.

5.Text: ...We often fought. He believed we would take after him. None of us did. And when the Fates decided that the time had come for us to rule in his stead... he resisted. Bitterly. But these old memories... I would leave them buried.

1.Text: Please hang on, Father. I have to safeguard the details, but... I'm getting closer to something... a way to stop Chronos. Forever.

2.Text: Forever... even when my brothers, foster-sisters, and I vanquished him... we knew he would eventually be back... a deathless Titan. But we thought... it would be on our terms. We were such fools.

3.Text: What else could you have done? He left you with no choice. And you lacked the means to destroy him utterly.

4.Text: It was for the best that we lacked such means... we would have used them and continued using them. I merely judge the dead, or used to... I was never fit to judge the living.

1.Text: To think that you might stop the Titan forever. In my youth I could not even believe we were related. Yet now I realize... I have grown old, and wretched, and wrathful... like him.

2.Text: Lord Father, it was my wrath that brought me to this point! And how can you possibly compare yourself? Look what the Titan did to you...

3.Text: We did this to {#Emph}each other! {#Prev}Gods and Titans... doomed to live forever, yet learn nothing all the while. Do as you must... but take no vengeance in my name.

1.Text: You have the Death Defiance. Runs in the family. Your brother Zagreus, he was also rather sturdy for his stature. Hard-headed, as a boy.

2.Text: Don't speak of him as though he's gone! Chronos has him, and Mother, and the rest. But when all this is over... we'll see each other again.

3.Text: How can you be so certain? To make such guarantees of the unknown! The Titan... my father... he shall not stop. He is the most hard-headed of us all.

1.Text: Cease with this foolishness, Daughter. There is no stopping him. He is inevitability itself.
You risk too much by visiting me here.
My son would never listen to me; I was a fool to think it a distinctive trait.
I've little strength of late, but you shall have it nonetheless.
Thank you for looking after Cerberus, though look after yourself.
You are as willful as your brother, aren't you...
Whenever you return... so does a portion of my strength.
Take no unnecessary risks and go unseen, Daughter.
You have vanquished the Titan before; you know full well what it takes.
I am of little use like this. You need not stray from your path on my account.
Hold nothing back against the Titan. That you are family matters not to him.
Be on your way, Daughter. I require no assistance here.
The Witch of the Crossroads swore no harm would come to you; ensure she keeps her word.
How strange to have a moment's peace with you and Cerberus, in such an age.
We have anticipated your arrival, ever since the dog bounded in here.
Go, take your vengeance. Our family, we've more than enough to spare.
He is no mere Titan. He is Time itself; and Time cannot be stopped...
These shackles sap me of my force of will; but not entirely.
This is not how I imagined my daughter would spend the evenings of her youth...

1.Speaker: NPC_Unnamed_01
1.Text: {#Emph}Pah! {#Prev}Another tormentor come to break me, or to try. And such a frail one, at that. Has the Titan Lord a lack for decent help?

2.Text: You... are you... the master of this beast?

3.Speaker: NPC_Unnamed_01
3.Text: {#Emph}The master of this beast? Ha, haha! {#Prev}Well, if I'm to be remembered, I could think of far worse ways than that. Though, this {#Emph}beast {#Prev}has yet to so much as snarl at you...

4.Text: {#Emph}<Gasp> {#Prev}Lord Hades, you're my.... Father, I'm... Melinoë. I'm your daughter.

5.Text: ...My daughter. Melinoë? Merciful Fates...! You cannot be here. He shall find you. He'll find you, and...

6.Text: ...I'll slay him where he stands. Where is he?

7.Text: He's in my blasted House! Where you were meant to be, and I. Look at me, Daughter. I could not confront him on my own. What do you expect shall happen?

8.Text: I expect he'll underestimate me. Father, let me free you from these bonds!

9.Text: {#Emph}No! {#Prev}No, that would bring greater ruin, nothing more. Now, get out of this place. Though let me lend to you what strength I still possess.
